22:1: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty says: O people, beware of the punishment of your Lord by obeying Him, so obey Him and do not disobey Him, for His punishment for those He punishes on the Day of Resurrection is severe. Then God Almighty described the horror of the signs of that Day and its beginnings, saying: Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing. Scholars differed about the time of the earthquake that God Almighty described as severe. Some of them said: It will occur in this world before the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, regarding his statement, Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing, he said: before the Hour. Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Amer: “O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing.” He said: This is in this world before the Day of Resurrection. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, The earthquake of the Hour, he said: Its earthquake: its signs... the verses, “On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget her nursing mother, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and you will see the people as if they were drunk, but they are not drunk.” Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Amer: “O people, fear your Lord. Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing.” He said: This is one of the signs of the Hour in this world. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a manner similar to what these people said. There is a report in its chain of transmission that is questionable, and that is what: Abu Kuraib told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the trumpet and gave it to Israfil, who is placing it on his mouth, staring at the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded. Abu Hurairah said: O Messenger of God, what are the images? He said: A horn. He said: What is it like? He said: A great horn in which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of the stun, and the third is the blast of the rising of the Lord of the Worlds. God Almighty commands Israfil with the first blast, and he says: Blow the blast of terror, and the people of the heavens and the earth will be terrified except for whom God wills, and God commands him to continue it and prolong it, and it will not cease. It is the one about which God says: These people do not await except a single blast that will have no stopping (Surah Sad: 15). God moves the mountains, and they become a mirage, and the earth shakes with its people in a great tremor. It is the one about which God says: The Day the great earthquake will shake, followed by another, hearts that Day will be trembling (Surah al-Nazi’at 79:6-8). The earth will be like a ship that is destroyed in the sea, struck by waves, and its people will be overturned, or like a lamp suspended from the throne, swayed by the spirits, and the people will sway on its back, and the nursing mothers will be stunned, the pregnant women will give birth, the children will turn gray, and the devils will fly away until they reach the regions. The angels will meet them, and they will strike their faces, and they will return, and the people will turn back, calling to one another, and He is the One Who will say, “The Day of Calling, the Day when you will turn back, you will have no protector from God. And he whom God sends astray, for him there is no guide.” Ghafir 32-33 While they were in that state, the earth cracked from one region to another, and they saw a tremendous matter, and they were seized by that with distress that God knows best. Then they looked at the sky, and behold, it was like molten metal, then its sun was eclipsed and its moon was eclipsed, and its stars were scattered, then they were removed from them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The dead do not know anything about that. Abu Hurairah said: Who did God except when He says: So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth was terrified, except whom God willed (al-Naml 27:87)? He said: Those are the martyrs, and the terror only reaches the living. They are alive with their Lord, provided for. God protected them from the terror of that Day and made them feel safe. It is the punishment of God that He sends upon the worst of His creation, and He is the One Who says: “O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing.”... to His saying: But the punishment of God is severe. This statement that we mentioned about Alqamah and Al-Sha’bi and those we mentioned about him, is a statement had it not been for the arrival of authentic reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that contradict it, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more knowledgeable about the meanings of God’s revelation and His sending down. The correct thing to say about that is: what is authentically reported from him. Mentioning the narration from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as we mentioned. Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam told me: Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of a companion of his who told him, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, who said: “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on one of his campaigns, and he had missed the march with his companions, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out with this verse: ‘O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing.’ So they urged the mounts until they were around the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Do you know what day that is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: That is the day when Adam will call out, his Lord will call out to him: ‘Send forth the people of Hell, from every thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine to Hell.’ So the people were in despair, and none of them laughed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Do you not work and be glad, for with you are two creatures that were never with a people except that they multiplied. Those who perished from the children of Adam, and those who perished from the children of Iblis and Gog and Magog.’ He said: ‘Be glad.’ You are among people like a mole on the side of a camel, or a mark on the wing of an animal. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Yahya ibn Saeed told us: Hisham ibn Abi Abdullah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Bashar told us: Muadh ibn Hisham told us: My father told us, and Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hisham, all of them, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Abu Kuraib told us: Muhammad bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Ziyad, on the authority of Imran, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Awf told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: “It reached me that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were with him after he approached Medina, he recited: ‘O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing. The Day you see it. ’... the verse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Do you know what day that is? ’ It was said: ‘God and His Messenger know best. ’ He mentioned something similar, except that he added: ‘And there were no two Messengers except that there was a period of ignorance between them, so they are the people of the Fire. And you are among two creatures whom no one on earth will oppose except for their great numbers, and they are Gog and Magog, and they are the people of the Fire, and the number of hypocrites will be completed. ’” Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Mas’udi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “It will be said to Adam: ‘Bring forth the people of Hell.’ He will say: ‘And what are the people of Hell?’ He will say: ‘Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.’ At that time, the young will turn gray, the pregnant woman will give birth, and you will see the people drunk, but they are not drunk, but the punishment of God is severe. We said: ‘Then where is the one who will be saved, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘Be glad, for one of you and a thousand of Gog and Magog.’ Then he said: ‘I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise.’ So we said: ‘God is great and praised God.’ Then he said: ‘I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise.’ So we said: ‘God is great and praised God.’ Then he said: ‘I hope that you will be half the people of Paradise. Your example among the people is like a white hair on a black bull, or like a black hair on a white bull.’” Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will say to Adam on the Day of Resurrection, then he mentioned something similar. Isa bin Othman bin Isa Al-Ramli told me: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the gathering. He said: God will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:O Adam. He will say: At your service and at your pleasure, and goodness is in your hands. He will say: Send a group to the Fire.” Then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: "O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing"... until The punishment of God is severe... the verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on a journey, and his voice echoed with it until his companions came back to him, and he said: Do you know what day this is? This is the day when God will say to Adam: O Adam, arise and send forth the people of Hell, from every thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine. This was difficult for the Muslims, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Go forth and come near and be glad, for by the One in Whose hand is my soul, you are among people like a mole on the side of a camel, or like a mark on the forearm of an animal. And with you are two creatures who have never been in anything except that they have multiplied it: Gog and Magog and those who perished from among the disbelieving jinn and mankind." Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: I entered upon Ibn Mas’ud at the treasury, and he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Would you be pleased to be a quarter of the people of Paradise? We said: Yes. He said: Would you be pleased to be a third of the people of Paradise? We said: Yes. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise, and I will tell you about that. No one will enter Paradise except a Muslim soul, and the small number of Muslims among the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection will be like a black hair on a white bull, or like a white hair on a black bull. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing, he said: This is the Day of Resurrection. And the earthquake is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: The earth shook so-and-so, I shook it with an earthquake and a earthquake, with a kasra on the zay from the earthquake, as God said: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake (al-Zalzalah 99:1). Likewise the verbal noun from every sound verb if it comes in the form of faghlal, with a kasra on the first letter, such as waswasah, waswasah, and waswasah. If it is a noun, it is with a fatha on the first letter, earthquake and waswasah, and it is what whispered to the person, as the poet said: The ignorant and misguided person knows that time is full of calamities and earthquakes. And the Most High said: On the Day you see it, God Almighty says: On the Day you see, O people, the earthquake of the Hour, the magnitude of which will make every nursing mother forget what she was nursing. And what He means by His saying will forget is that she will forget and abandon herself due to the intensity of her distress. It is said: I forgot about such-and-such, I forgot about it, I forgot about it, and I also forgot. It is rare, and the eloquent is the opening of the ha’. As for the future tense, the ha’ is open in both languages. Nothing else has been heard, and from it is the saying of the poet: His heart woke up, O Ezz, or he almost went crazy If it is meant that the terror made him forget and consoled him, I said: This matter made him forget something, it made him completely astonished. And in proving the ha’ in his statement: every wet nurse, there is a difference of opinion among the Arab scholars. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: If the ha’ is proven in the word wildered woman, then what is meant is the mother of the breastfeeding boy, and if it is omitted, then what is meant is the woman who is breastfeeding a boy with her, that the action is meant by her. They said: If the description was meant by her, as he sees it, he would have said wildered woman. He said: Likewise, every passive participle or fa’il that is for the female, but not for the male, is without the ha’, such as: muqarrab, “muwaqqar,” mushaddan, “hamil,” and ha’idh. Abu Ja`far said: This statement, in my opinion, is more correct in this regard, because it is the custom of the Arabs to drop the feminine ta’ from every fa’il and fa’il, if they describe a feminine with it, even if the masculine has no share in it. So if they wanted to report that she will do it, but she will not do it, they would add the feminine ta’ to differentiate between the adjective and the verb. From this is the saying of al-A’sha about what is happening, but had not happened before: Oh neighbor between me, you are divorced, such are the affairs of people, come and go As for what is an adjective, such as the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: Like you, a pregnant woman who has been knocked on the door, and a nursing mother who has been distracted by a man with amulets They may have confirmed the letter ha in both cases, and they may have dropped it in both cases, but the eloquent part of their speech is what I have described. The interpretation of the words then is: On the Day when you, O people, will see the earthquake of the Hour, every mother who breastfeeds her child will forget and abandon what she breastfed. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she nursed, he said: She will leave her child because of the distress that has befallen her. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Every nursing mother will forget what she nursed. He said: She will forget her children without weaning them. And every pregnant woman will drop her burden. He said: The pregnant women will cast off what was in their bellies before it was completed. And every pregnant woman will drop her burden. He said: And every pregnant woman will miscarry from the severity of the distress of her pregnancy. And his saying: And you will see the people drunk, the readers of the regions read And you will see the people drunk as a direct address to one person, as if he said: And you will see, O Muhammad, the people drunk at that time, but they are not drunk. It has been narrated on the authority of Abu Zaza’ah bin Amr bin Jarir, And you will see the people with a damma on the ta’ and an accusative on the naas, from the saying of the speaker: Have you seen, you will see, which requires a noun and a verb, like think and its sisters. The correct reading of this, according to us, is what the readers of the countries have said, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers on it. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement: drunkards. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa read it: drunkards, but they are not drunk. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it: You see the people drunk, but they are not drunk. The correct thing to say about this, according to us, is that they are two widely used readings in the readings of the regions, and they are close in meaning. So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. The meaning of the statement is: And you see the people, O Muhammad, from the great distress and severity that has befallen them, drunk with fear, but they are not drunk from drinking wine. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us: Al-Hussein told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And you see the people drunk from fear, but they are not drunk from drinking. Al-Husayn said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: And they are not drunk, he said: They are not drunk from drinking, but the punishment of God is severe. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And you see the people drunk, but they are not drunk, he said: They did not drink wine. But the punishment of God is severe, God Almighty says: But they became drunk from fear of the punishment of God when they witnessed what they witnessed of the distress of that and the enormity of its horror, despite their knowledge of the severity of the punishment of God.
22:2: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and you will see the people as if they were drunk, but they are not drunk. Rather, the punishment of God is severe.”
22:3: It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge. He said: Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith. What he means by his statement: He who disputes about God without knowledge is he who disputes about God, claiming that God is unable to revive someone who has decayed and turned to dust, without knowledge that he knows, rather out of ignorance of what he is saying, and follows in his saying that and his dispute about God without knowledge, every rebellious devil.
22:4: God Almighty says: The devil has been decreed, so the meaning of was decreed here is was decreed, and the ha in His statement upon him is from the mention of the devil. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: It was written for him that whoever follows him he said: It was written for Satan that whoever follows Satan from among God’s creation. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: It was decreed for him that whoever takes him as a friend, he said: Satan followed him. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated: Mujahid narrated: Whoever takes him as a friend, he said: Follow him. And His statement: Then he will mislead him means: The devil will mislead him, meaning: He will mislead whoever takes him as a friend. The ha in will mislead him refers back to whoever in His statement: Whoever takes him as a friend. The interpretation of the statement is that it has been decreed that the devil will mislead his followers and will not guide them to the truth. And His statement: And will guide him to the punishment of the Blaze means: And he will drive whoever follows him to the punishment of the blazing Hell. And His driving him to it is by calling him to obey Him and disobey the Most Merciful, so that is His guidance of whoever follows him to the punishment of Hell. The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection - then indeed We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, some formed and some unformed, that We may make clear to you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, then [you will] reach your [full] maturity.” This is an argument from God against the one who was told about the people that he argues about God without knowledge, following the rebellious Satan, and alerting him to the place of error in what he said, and his denial of what he denied of the power of his Lord. He said: O people, if you are in doubt about Our ability to resurrect you and your graves after your death and your affliction, because you are astonished by that, then in Our beginning We created your father Adam from dust, then We created you from the sperm of Adam, then We changed you in states, state after state, from sperm to clot, then from clot to lump of flesh, for you is a lesson and admonition from which you may learn, so that you may know that He who is able to do that is unable to bring you back after your annihilation, as you were alive before annihilation. The people of interpretation differed regarding his statement, created and uncreated. Some of them said: It is from the description of the sperm. He said: The meaning of that is: We created you from dust, then from a sperm, created and uncreated. They said: As for the created, it is what was a sound creation. As for the uncreated, it is what the wombs expelled from the sperm and expelled before it was created. Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Aamir, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: When the sperm-drop falls into the womb, God sends an angel who says: O Lord, is it formed or unformed? If he says: Unformed, the wombs expel it as blood. If he says: Formed, He says: O Lord, what is the description of this sperm-drop? Is it male or female? What is its sustenance? What is its life span? Is it miserable or happy? He said: Then it is said to him: Go to the Mother of the Book and copy from it the description of this sperm-drop. He said: The angel then goes and copies it, and it remains with him until he reaches its final description. Others said: The meaning of this is: complete and incomplete. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Sulayman told us, he said: Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the statement of God: created and uncreated, he said: complete and incomplete. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Qatada: Created and uncreated. Then he mentioned something similar. Others said: The meaning of this is that the embryo is shaped as a human being and not shaped. So if it is shaped, it is created, and if it is not shaped, it is not created. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: formed, he said: The miscarriage is formed and not formed. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: created and uncreated. He said: The miscarriage is created and uncreated. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, that he said about the sperm and the lump of flesh, if it is reversed in the fourth creation, it is a created soul, and if he ejaculates it before that, it is not created. He said: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Abi Salamah, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah: Created and uncreated. He said: The miscarriage. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The created means the one who has been fully formed, and uncreated means the miscarriage before its full creation, because the created and uncreated are descriptions of the lump of flesh and the sperm after it becomes a lump of flesh, nothing remains for it until it becomes a normal creation except the formation, and that is what is meant by his saying: created and uncreated a normal creation, and uncreated means that the mother gives birth to it as a lump of flesh and it is not formed, and the soul is not breathed into it. And His saying: To make clear to you means, the Most High said: We made the embryo from it the fully formed one, and from it the imperfect aborted one, to make clear to you Our ability to do whatever We will, and to make you aware of the beginning of Your creation. And His statement: And We establish in the wombs whom We will for a specified term. God Almighty says: Whoever We have decreed to remain and live for a term and an end, We establish him in his mother’s womb until the time that We have appointed for him to remain in her womb, so that she does not miscarry him, nor does he leave her until he reaches his term. Then when he reaches the time for his exit from her womb, We permit him to exit from her, so he exits. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And We establish in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, he said: Completion. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We place in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, he said: The specified term is his residence in the womb until he emerges. And His statement: Then We bring you out as a child, God Almighty says: Then We bring you out from the wombs of your mothers when you have reached the term that I have determined for you to emerge from them as small children. And He made the word child singular, and it is an attribute of all, because it is a source like justice and falsehood. And his saying: Then that you may reach your full strength means: Then that you may reach the perfection of your minds and the fullness of your powers in your life. I have mentioned the disagreement of those who disagree about the most severe, and the correct statement about it according to us with its evidence in what has passed, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
22:5: God the Almighty says: And among you, O people, is he who dies before reaching his prime, and among you is he whose life span is prolonged, so he lives until he becomes very old, and he returns after the end of his youth and reaching the peak of his prime to the most decrepit of his age, and that decrepitude is until he returns to his state in his youth, not understanding anything after his first understanding. The meaning of the words: And among you is he who returns to the most decrepit of his age after reaching his prime, so that he does not know, after the knowledge he used to know, anything. And His statement: And you see the earth lifeless, God the Almighty says: And you see the earth, O Muhammad, dry, with traces of plants and crops gone, and the root of humud is destruction and ruin, and it is said from it: the earth has become humud, humud, and from it is the saying of Al-A'sha Maymun bin Qais: Qatila said: Why is your body pale and I see your clothes worn out with grief? Al-Hamd is the plural of Hamid, just as Al-Ruk’ is the plural of Raki’. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, And you see the earth barren, he said: There is vegetation in it. And His statement: So when We send down upon it water, it quivers, God Almighty says: So when We send down upon this lifeless land in which there is no vegetation, rain from the sky, it quivers: He says: It moves with the vegetation, and swells, He says: And weakens the vegetation with the coming of the rain. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: It shook and swayed. He said: He knew the rain in its hills. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: It shook and swelled. He said: It became beautiful, and the rain was known in its hills. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Then when We send down water upon it, it shakes, and the meaning is directed to the crops, even though the speech is directed to the report of the earth. The readers of the regions read and it grew with the meaning of: growth, which is growth and increase. Abu Ja`far al-Qari’ used to read that and and it grew with a hamza. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Farra’, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Tamimi, on his authority. This is a mistake, because there is no meaning for Lord here. Rather, it is said: Raba’a with a hamza, meaning: guarded from rabi’ah, and there is no meaning for guarding in this place. The correct reading is what the readers of the regions are upon. And His saying: And it produced from every beautiful pair, God Almighty says: And this lifeless land produced from that rain, from every beautiful type. By beautiful, He means: delight, which is beauty. And in a manner similar to what we said about humiliation, as the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And it produces from every beautiful pair. He said: Good. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same.
22:6: He, the Most High, means by His saying, That: This is what I have mentioned to you, O people, since We began to create you in the wombs of your mothers, and We described your conditions before and after birth, as a child, an adult, and an old man, and We alerted you to Our actions with the lifeless earth by sending down rain upon it so that you may believe and acknowledge that the One Who did that is God, Who is the Truth, there is no doubt about it, and that what you worship other than Him of idols and statues is false because they are not able to do any of that, and you may know that the power with which He made these wondrous things, it is not impossible for Him to revive the dead after their annihilation and their being eroded in the dust, and that the Doer of that is capable of everything He wills and desires, nothing He wills is impossible for Him, and so that you may be certain of that, that the Hour in which I promised you that I would raise the dead from their graves will inevitably come, there is no doubt about it. He says: There is no doubt about its coming and occurrence. And that God will resurrect those in the graves at that time, those in the graves who are dead, alive to the place of reckoning, so do not doubt that, and do not dispute it.
22:7: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that God will resurrect those in the graves.
22:8: God Almighty says: And among the people is he who disputes about the Oneness of God and His singling out Him as God, without knowledge of what he disputes about, nor guidance, meaning: and he changes the explanation of what he says, nor proof, nor an enlightening book, meaning: and without a book from God that came to him to prove the truth of what he says out of ignorance, based on his assumption and calculation. He mentioned that he meant by this verse and the one after it Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith from Banu Abd Al-Dar.
22:9: God Almighty says: This one who argues about God argues without knowledge. Second, his conjunction. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning for which he was described as bending his elbows, and what was meant by describing him with that. Some of them said: He described him with that for his arrogance and swagger. It was mentioned from the Arabs that they say: So-and-so came to me bending his elbows, if he came swaggering with arrogance. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, His second affection, he said: arrogant in himself. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He cut off his neck. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, the second of his neck, he said: his neck. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The second of his neck. He said: No, and his neck. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, similarly. Others said: This means that he turns away from what he is called to and does not listen to him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, He turns away from mentioning Me, meaning: He turns away from mentioning Me. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: He turned his head away to mislead from the path of God. He said: He turned his head away, turning away, not wanting to hear what was said to him. And he recited: And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn their heads away, and you see them turning away while they are arrogant. (al-Munafiqun 63:5) And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly. (Luqman 31:7) Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, The second of his turning away, he said: He turns away from the truth. Abu Jaafar said: These three statements are close in meaning, because whoever is arrogant, it is his nature to turn away from what he is arrogant about, turn his neck away from it and turn away. The correct thing to say about this is that God described this disputant about God as not knowing, because of his arrogance, when he is called to God, he turns away from his caller, turns his neck away from him, and does not listen to what is said to him out of arrogance. And His statement, to mislead from the path of God, the Most High says: This polytheist argues about God without knowledge, turning away from the truth out of arrogance, to turn the believers in God away from the religion to which He has guided them, and to cause them to slip away from it. For him in this world is disgrace, the Most High says: For this one who argues about God without knowledge, in this world is disgrace, which is killing, humiliation, and disgrace at the hands of the believers, so God killed him by their hands on the day of Badr. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his saying, In this world there is disgrace, he said: He was killed on the day of Badr. And His statement, And We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning Fire, means, And We will burn him on the Day of Resurrection with the Fire. And His statement, That is because of what your hands have put forth, means, And it will be said to him when he tastes the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, “This punishment that We will make you taste today is because of what your hands have put forth in this world of sins and crimes, and what you have acquired in it of crimes.” And that God is not unjust to the servants, means, “And We did that because God is not unjust to the servants, so He punishes some of His servants for a crime while He forgives the same of another other than him, or He holds the sin of a sinner accountable to another other than him, so He punishes him for it and pardons the one who committed the sin, but He does not punish anyone except for his crime, and He does not punish anyone for a sin the like of which He forgives for another except for a reason by which he deserves His forgiveness.
22:10: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: That is because of what your hands have put forth and because God is not unjust to His servants.
22:11: He, the Most High, meant by His saying, And among the people is he who worships God on the verge, that they were Arabs who used to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as emigrants from their desert. If they attained ease of living after the emigration and entering Islam, they would remain in Islam, otherwise they would turn back on their heels. So God said, And among the people is he who worships God on the verge of doubt. But if good befalls him, he is content therewith, which is ease of living and what is similar to it from the causes of this world, he is content therewith. He says: He settled in Islam and remained steadfast upon it, then he turned back upon the path he had been upon, which was disbelief in God. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And among the people is he who worships God on the edge… to His statement, turns back on his face. He said: The trial is the affliction. When one of them came to Madinah, which was a land and a place of safety, and his body was healthy there, and his mare gave birth to a beautiful foal, and his wife gave birth to a boy, he was pleased with him and felt secure with him and said: I have not attained anything since I have been upon this religion of mine except good. But if the pain of Madinah afflicted him, and his wife gave birth to a girl, and the zakat was delayed from him, Satan would come to him and say: By God, I have not attained anything since I have been upon this religion of yours except evil, and that is the trial. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahmad ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And among the people is he who worships God on the edge, he said: on doubt. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, on the edge, he said: on doubt. If good befalls him, ease and well-being, he is reassured by it: he settles down. And if a trial befalls him, torment and calamity, he turns back, he turns back, turns back, “on his face,” a disbeliever. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Ibn Jurayj said: There were people from the Arab tribes and from the people of the villages around them who would say: We will go to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and if we find a better livelihood, we will stay with him, and if not, we will go back to our people. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Whoever worships God on the edge of doubt, he said, if good befalls him, meaning: his wealth increases, and his livestock increases, he is reassured and says: Nothing has befallen me in this religion of mine since I entered it except good. But if a trial befalls him, meaning: if his wealth is lost, and his livestock is lost, he turns on his face, losing this world and the Hereafter. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding the words of God, And among mankind is he who worships God on the edge Al-Baqarah 2:176: There were people from the tribes of the Arabs and from the villages around Medina who used to say: Let us go to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and look into his affair. If we encounter goodness, we will remain with him, and if not, we will return to our homes and families. They used to come to him and say: We follow your religion. If they were able to make a living, and their horses were successful, and their women gave birth to boys, they would be reassured and say: This is a true religion. But if their provision was delayed, and their horses slipped, and their women gave birth to girls, they would say: This is an evil religion, and they turned back on their faces. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, “And of the people is he who worships God on the edge. If good befalls him, he is content therewith; but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He loses this world and the Hereafter.” He said: This is the hypocrite. If his worldly affairs are good for him, he continues in worship, but if his worldly affairs are corrupted and changed, he turns back, and he does not continue in worship except for what is good in his worldly affairs. And if a hardship or trial, or test or distress befalls him, he abandons his religion and returns to disbelief. And His statement, He has lost this world and the Hereafter, means: This one, whose description is described by the Most High, has been deprived of his worldly life, because he did not obtain what he needed from it due to his worship of God based on doubt, and he was put to the test in his trade and did not profit. And the Hereafter, meaning: He has lost the Hereafter, for he will be tormented in it by the kindled Fire of God. And His statement, That is the manifest loss, means: And his loss of this world and the Hereafter is the loss, meaning the manifest destruction, meaning it is clear to whoever thinks about it and ponders it that he has lost this world and the Hereafter. The reciters differed in their reading of this. All the reciters of the countries, except Hamid al-A’raj, read it as loser of this world and the hereafter in the past tense. Hamid al-A’raj read it as loser in the accusative case as a state, on the model of fa’il.
22:12: God Almighty says: And if a trial befalls this one who worships God on the edge of temptation, he will turn away from the religion of God, calling upon gods besides God who will not harm him if he does not worship them in this world, nor will they benefit him in the Hereafter if he worships them. That is the extreme error. He says: His apostasy, calling upon these gods besides God, is taking it in a wrong direction, and going far away from the religion of God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He calls upon besides God that which neither harms him nor benefits him, he disbelieves after his belief. That is the farthest error.
22:13: God Almighty says: This one who has turned his face away from a trial calls upon gods whose harm to him in the Hereafter is closer and quicker to him than their benefit. It was mentioned that Ibn Masoud used to recite it: He calls upon those whose harm is closer than their benefit. The Arabists differed about the position of min. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Its position is in the accusative case of yad’u. He said: Its meaning is: He calls upon gods whose harm is closer than their benefit. He said: It is irregular because yad’u li Zayd was not found in the speech. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The lam of the conjunction of what comes after min, as if the meaning of the speech according to him is: He calls upon someone whose harm is closer than his benefit. He narrated from the Arabs what they heard from them: I have what is better for someone else than him, meaning: I have what is better for someone else than him. And I gave you what is better for someone else than him, meaning: What is better for someone else than him. He said: It is permissible in everything in which the inflection is not clear to interrupt with the lam without the noun. Others among them said: It is possible that the meaning of that is: He calls for the distant misguidance, so that calls is the connection of the distant misguidance, and the ha’ is implied in calls, then you resume the speech with the lam, so you say to someone whose harm is closer than his benefit: Labasa al-mawla, like your saying in the speech in the doctrine of recompense for what you did is better for you. So according to this statement, min is in the nominative case with the ha’ in his statement Dharah, because if min is a recompense, then what comes after it parses it, and the second lam in Labasa al-mawla is the answer to the first lam. This other statement according to the doctrine of Arabic is more correct, and the first is closer to the doctrine of the people of interpretation. And his saying, What a bad master means: What a bad cousin is this who worships God. On the letter and what a bad companion means: What a bad companion and friend he is, as: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, And what an evil companion he is, he said: The companion is the companion and friend. It has been said: What is meant by the master in this place is the supportive guardian. Mujahid used to say: What he meant by his saying, What a bad master and what a bad companion, was the idol. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And what an evil companion it is, he said: The idol.
22:14: God Almighty says: Indeed, God will admit those who believed in God and His Messenger, and did what He commanded them in this world, and refrained from what He forbade them from therein, into gardens: meaning orchards with rivers flowing beneath them meaning rivers flow beneath their trees. Indeed, God does what He wills so He gives whatever He wills of His honor to those who obey Him, and whatever He wills of humiliation to those who disobey Him.
22:15: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the letter ha’ in His statement, that God will not support him. Some of them said: It refers to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he interpreted it according to the saying of some of those who said that: Whoever among the people thinks that God will not support Muhammad in this world and the next, let him extend a rope, which is the rope, to the sky: meaning the sky of the House, which is its roof, then let him cut off the rope after suffocating with it, then let him see whether that suffocation will remove his anger, and cutting off the rope after suffocation will remove what angers him: he says: Will that remove what anger he feels in his chest? Who said that? Nasr bin Ali told us, he said: My father told me, he said: Khalid bin Qais told me, on the authority of Qatada: Whoever thinks that God will not support His Prophet, His religion, or His Book, let him extend a rope meaning: a rope to the sky of the House and choke on it, and let him see whether his plot will remove that which enrages him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Thawr, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Whoever thinks that God will not support him in this world and the Hereafter, he said: Whoever thinks that God will not support His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, let him extend a rope meaning: a rope to the sky of the House, then let him cut meaning: then let him choke himself, then let him see if his plot will remove what enrages him. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. Others who said the letter ha in yanasruhu from the mention of the name of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sky mentioned in this place is the well-known sky. They said: The meaning of the words is: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Whoever thinks that God will not support him in this world and the Hereafter, then he recited it until he reached, Will his plot remove that which enrages him? He said, “Whoever thinks that God will not support his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and struggles to do this matter in order to cut it off from him, and from it: let him cut it off from its origin from where it comes, for its origin is in the heavens, so let him extend a path to the heavens, then let him cut off from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the revelation that comes to him from God, for he will not struggle with it until he cuts off its origin from him, so he plotted against that until he cut off its origin from him. “Let him see whether his plot removes that which enrages him,” what entered them from that, and God enraged them with it from supporting the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what was revealed to him. Others who said that the ha’ in his statement supports him from the mention of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the meaning of support here is provision, so according to what these people say the interpretation of the statement is: Whoever thinks that God will not provide for Muhammad in this world, and will not give him. And they mentioned what was heard from the Arabs: Whoever supports me, God will support him, meaning: Whoever gives to me, God will give to him. And they also ruled, according to what they heard: The rain supported such-and-such land: if it made it generous and revived it, and evidence for that was the verse of Al-Faq’asi: You do not give a man more than he deserves, nor do you own the part that the rain supports. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Atiyah told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: What do you think of his statement, “Whoever thinks that God will not support him in this world and the Hereafter, let him stretch out a rope to the heaven and then let it be cut off and see whether his plot will remove that which enrages him.” He said: Whoever thinks that God will not support Muhammad, let him tie a rope to the ceiling and then strangle himself with it until he dies. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani, on the authority of al-Tamimi, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about his statement: Whoever thinks that God will not support him, he said: That God will not provide for him in this world and the Hereafter. Then let him stretch out a rope to the sky, and the rope is the rope, and the sky is the roof of the house, so let him hang a rope in the sky of the house, then let him choke. Then let him see whether his plan will go away, this is what he did out of anger. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Mutawwaf, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man from Banu Tamim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Whoever thinks that God will not support him in this world and the Hereafter, let him stretch out a rope to the sky. He said: The sky of the House. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Dawud told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said: I heard Al-Tamimi say: I asked Ibn Abbas and he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Whoever thinks that God will not support him in this world and the Hereafter… to His statement, what enrages him, he said: The sky to which God commanded that a rope be extended because of the roof of the House, He commanded that a rope be extended to it so that he would be strangled by it. He said: So let him see if his plot will remove what enrages him if he is strangled, if he fears that God will not support him! Others said: The ha’ in yansuruh is mentioned by man. They said: The meaning of the statement is: Whoever thinks that God will not provide for him in this world and the hereafter, let him stretch out a rope to the heavens of the House, then let him choke, and let him see if his actions will remove that which angers him that he will not be provided for! Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, that God will not support him, he said: God will provide for him. Then let him extend a rope, he said: with a rope, to the sky, “the sky above you,” then let him cut it, “so that he may be strangled. Will his plot go away? That is his strangulation, so that he will not be provided for. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Whoever thinks that God will not support him, God will provide for him, let him extend a rope to the sky, he said: a rope to the sky. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: To the sky means to the sky of the House. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: Then let him cut off means: let him choke, and that is his trick that enrages him. He said: That is his choking so that God does not provide for him. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement, Then let him extend a rope meaning: a rope to the sky meaning: the sky of the House. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, he said: Ikrimah was asked about his statement, Then let him extend a rope to the sky, he said: The sky of the House, Then let him cut it off, he said: Let him be strangled. The most correct interpretation of this, in my opinion, is the statement of the one who said: The letter ha’ is from the mention of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his religion. This is because God, the Most High, mentioned a people who worship Him on the edge, and that they are reassured by the religion if they attain goodness in their worship of Him, and that they turn away from their religion because of a hardship that befalls them in it. Then He followed that with this verse. So it is known that He only followed it as a rebuke to them for their turning away from the religion, that their doubt in it is their hypocrisy, and their impatientness for ease in life, or abundance in provision. And if it was necessary for that to be after the report of their hypocrisy, then the meaning of the speech, since that was the case, is: Whoever thinks that God will not provide for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation in this world, and will not provide for them from His grace in it, and will not provide for them in the Hereafter from the years of His gifts and honor, because he is impatient for God to do that to him and to them, then let him extend a rope to the sky above him: either the roof of a house, or something else to which the cause is attached from above, then let him choke if he is angered by some of what God has decreed, and he hastens for that to be revealed to him, then let him see if his plot will go away with his choking, likewise what angers him, and if his anger does not go away, until God brings relief from Him and removes it, then likewise his hastening for God’s victory for Muhammad and his religion, he will not delay what God has decreed for him from that from its appointed time, nor will he hasten before its time. It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed about Asad and Ghatafan, who were slow to convert to Islam and said: We fear that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will not be victorious, and that which is between us and our allies from the Jews will be cut off, so that they will not provide us with provisions or water. So God Almighty said to them: Whoever hastens the victory of Muhammad from God, let him extend a rope to the sky and let him choke, and let him consider his haste in that within himself, does it relieve his anger? Likewise, his hastening the victory of Muhammad from God without bringing his victory forward before its time. The Arabists differed about what is in his saying what enrages. Some of the grammarians of Basra said that it means who, and he said: The meaning of the statement is: Will they afflict his guile which enrages him? He said: And the ha’ was deleted because it is the connection of who, because if they both became one noun, the deletion would be. Another said: Rather, it is a source that does not need the ha’, will they afflict his guile which enrages him? And His statement, And thus We have sent it down as clear signs, the Most High says: And just as I have made clear to you My arguments against those who deny My ability to revive those who have died from among creation after their annihilation, and I have made them clear, O people, thus We have sent down to Our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, this Qur’an as clear signs, meaning clear indications, guiding whomever God wills to the truth. And that God guides whomever He wills, the Most High says: And because God guides to the right path whomever He wills, He sent down this Qur’an as clear signs, so in is in the accusative case.
22:16: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And thus We have sent it down as clear signs, and indeed, God guides whom He wills.
22:17: God Almighty says: The separation between these hypocrites who worship God on the edge, and those who associated partners with God and worshipped idols and statues, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, Christians and Magians who glorified the fires and extinguished them, and those who believed in God and His messengers, is up to God, and He will separate between them on the Day of Resurrection with justice from judgment, and His separation between them is His entering the Fire of all the parties and Paradise of the believers in Him and His messengers, so that is the separation from God between them. Qatada said about this: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans or Magians or polytheists, he said: The Sabeans are a people who worship angels, pray toward the qiblah, and recite the Psalms. And the Magians worship the sun, the moon, and fire. And those who associate others with God: they worship idols. And the religions are six: five for Satan, and one for the Most Merciful. And the particle in was inserted into the predicate of the first in because of the meaning mentioned, and that the speech is in the sense of recompense, as if it was said: Whoever is on one of these religions, then separate what is between him and whoever opposes him for God. And the Arabs sometimes insert in into the predicate of in if the predicate of the first noun is in a noun added to its mention, so you say: Indeed, Abdullah, indeed, goodness is abundant with him, as the poet said: The Caliph, God has clothed him in a royal garment, in which good endings are hoped for. Al-Farra’ used to say: Whoever said this did not say: You are standing, nor You are standing, because You are standing, because the two names differed, so it was good to reject the first and make the second as if it were the subject, so it was good because of the difference and bad because of the agreement. And His statement, Indeed, God is Witness over all things, means that God is Witness over all the actions of these categories whom God, the Most High, mentioned, and other than that of all things, and nothing of that is hidden from Him. The statement in the interpretation of the statement of God Almighty: “Have you not seen that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures and many of the people? But many upon whom the punishment is justified.” God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, with your heart, and learned that to God prostrates those in the heavens of the angels, and those on the earth of creation from the jinn and others, and the sun, the moon, and the stars in the sky, and the mountains, the trees, and the beasts on the earth. And the prostration of that is its shadow when the sun rises upon it, and when it sets, when the shadow of each thing changes, then it is its prostration. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Have you not seen that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, and the moving creatures? He said: The shadows of all of this. As for the prostration of the sun, moon and stars, it is as follows: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday and Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Awf told us: I heard Abu al-`Aliyah al-Riyahi say: There is no star in the sky, nor sun, nor moon, but it prostrates to God when it sets, then it does not turn away until it is given permission, so it takes the right, and Muhammad added until it returns to its place of rising. And his saying, And many people, means: And many of the children of Adam prostrate, and they are the believers in God. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, And many upon whom the punishment is due is in apposition to his saying: And many of the people, and he is included among those whom God described as prostrating to Him, and his saying: The punishment is due upon him is a connection to many. If the second many were among those who were not included among those described as prostrating, he would have been raised by the pronoun referring to him in his saying: The punishment is due upon him. The meaning of the statement at that time would be: And many refused to prostrate, because his saying: The punishment is due upon him indicates disobedience to God and his refusal to prostrate, so he deserved the punishment because of that.
22:18: God Almighty says: And whoever God humiliates from among His creation, making him miserable, there is none to honor him with happiness that would make him happy, because all matters are in God’s hand. He guides whomever He wills to obey Him, and disappoints whomever He wills, and makes miserable whomever He wills, and makes happy whomever He loves. And His statement, Indeed, God does what He wills, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: Indeed, God does with His creation what He wills of humiliating whomever He wants to humiliate, and honoring whomever He wants to honor, because creation is His creation, and the matter is His matter. He is not questioned about what He does, but they are questioned. It has been mentioned that some of them read it so he has no honor meaning: so he has no honor, and that is a reading that I do not permit reading with, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters to the contrary.
22:19: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of these two opponents that God mentioned. Some of them said: One of the two groups is the people of faith, and the other group is the idol worshippers from the polytheists of Quraysh who fought on the day of Badr. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Abu Hashim told us, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Qais bin Ubadah, he said: I heard Abu Dharr swear an oath that this verse, These two are opponents who have disputed about their Lord, was revealed about those who fought on the day of Badr: Hamza, Ali, Ubaidah bin Al-Harith, Utbah, Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah, and Al-Walid bin Utbah. He said: And Ali said: I am the first, or one of the first, to kneel in dispute on the Day of Resurrection before God, the Blessed and Most High. Ali bin Sahl told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Qais bin Ibad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swear by God an oath: This verse was revealed about six of the Quraysh 106:Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib, Ali bin Abi Talib, Ubaidah bin Al-Harith, may God be pleased with them, Utbah bin Rabi’ah, Shaibah bin Rabi’ah, and Al-Walid bin Utbah. These two are opponents who have disputed about their Lord... to the end of the verse. Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to the end of the verse. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Qais ibn Ibad, he said: I heard Abu Dharr swearing, then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Muhibb told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur ibn al-Mu’tamir, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yasaf: He said: This verse was revealed about those who fought on the day of Badr: These two are opponents who have disputed about their Lord. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar, who said: These verses were revealed: These two are opponents who have disputed about their Lord about those who fought on the day of Badr: Hamza, Ali, Ubaydah ibn al-Harith, Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi’ah, and al-Walid ibn Utbah. Up to His saying: And they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy. He said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Qais ibn Ubad, who said: By God, this verse was revealed: These two are opponents who have disputed about their Lord about those who went out to one another on the day of Badr: Hamza, Ali, Ubaydah, may God have mercy on them, Shaibah, Utbah, and Al-Walid ibn Utbah. Others who said that one of the two groups is the group of faith said: Rather, the other group is the People of the Book. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, These two are opponents who dispute about their Lord, he said: They are the People of the Book. They said to the believers: We are closer to God and have an earlier Book than you, and our Prophet was before your Prophet. And the believers said: We are more worthy of God. We believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we believe in your Prophet, and in what God has revealed of the Book. So you know our Book and our Prophet, then you abandoned it and disbelieved in it out of envy, and that was their dispute about their Lord. Others among them said: Rather, the other group are all infidels, whatever their religion. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, and Ata’ bin Abi Riyah, and Abu Qaz’ah, on the authority of Al-Hussein, he said: They are the disbelievers and the believers who disputed about their Lord. He said: Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: The example of the unbeliever and the believer. Ibn Jurayj said: Their dispute with which they disputed about their Lord is their dispute in this world from the people of every religion. They see that they are more deserving of God than others. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, he said: Asim and Al-Kalbi both used to say in These are two opponents who have disputed about their Lord, he said: The people of polytheism and Islam when they disputed about which of them was better, he said: He made polytheism a religion. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, - and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, These are two opponents who dispute about their Lord, he said: The example of the believer and the disbeliever is their dispute about the resurrection. Others said: The two opponents mentioned by God in this verse are Heaven and Hell. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, These are two opponents who disputed about their Lord. He said: They are Paradise and Hell. They disputed, and Hell said: God created me for His punishment, and Paradise said: God created me for His mercy. So God has related to you of their story what you hear. The first of these sayings to me to be correct, and the most similar to the interpretation of the verse, is the saying of the one who said: He meant by the two opponents: all the disbelievers of all kinds of disbelief and all the believers. I only said that it is more correct because the Most High mentioned before that two kinds of His creation: one of them is the people of obedience to Him by prostrating to Him, and the other: the people of disobedience to Him, for whom the punishment has been justified. He said: Do you not see that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun and the moon? Then He said: And many of the people, and many upon whom the punishment has been justified. Then He followed that with a description of both kinds and what He will do with them, so He said: Then those who disbelieved, garments of fire will be cut out for them. And God said: Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. So it was clear from that that what is between that is report about them. If someone says: What do you say about what was narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr regarding his statement that this was revealed about those who fought on the day of Badr? It is said: That is, God willing, as was narrated on his authority. However, the verse may have been revealed for a reason, then it is general for everything that was similar to that reason, and this is one of those. That is because those who fought, one of the two groups was people of polytheism and disbelief in God, and the other was people of faith in God and obedience to Him. So every disbeliever is like the group of polytheists in that he is an opponent to the people of faith, and likewise every believer, every believer, is like the group of faith in that he is an opponent to the people of polytheism. The interpretation of the statement: These are two opponents who disputed over the religion of their Lord, and their dispute over that is the enmity of each group towards the other group, and its war against it over its religion. And His statement, As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them. God Almighty says: As for the one who disbelieves in God among them, a shirt of copper from fire will be cut out for him. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them. He said: The disbeliever will have garments of fire cut out for him, and the believer will be admitted by God to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, regarding his statement, As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them. He said: Garments of copper, and there is no vessel hotter or more intense than it. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The unbelievers will have garments of fire cut out for them, but the believer will enter gardens beneath which rivers flow. And His statement, Pouring boiling water will be poured over their heads, means: Boiling water will be poured over their heads. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Zayd, on the authority of Abu al-Samh, on the authority of Ibn Juhayrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The boiling water will be poured over their heads, and it will penetrate their skulls until it reaches their stomachs, and what is in their stomachs will melt until it reaches their feet, and it will be melted, then it will be returned to how it was.” Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me: Ya`mar ibn Bishr told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us: Sa`id ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Abu al-Samh, on the authority of Ibn Juhayrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar, except that he said: It will penetrate the skull until it reaches his stomach, and what is in his stomach will be shed. Some of them claimed that his statement, And for them are maces of iron, is from the deferred meaning of the forward, and he said: The point of the statement is: As for those who disbelieved, garments of fire were cut out for them, and for them are maces of iron, and boiling water is poured over their heads. And he said: It is only necessary that this be so, because the angel strikes him with the iron mace until his head is pierced, then the boiling water is poured into him, the heat of which has reached its peak, and it cuts his stomach. And the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that we mentioned indicates the opposite of what this speaker said, and that is that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed that when the boiling water is poured over their heads, it penetrates the skull until it reaches their stomachs, and thus came the interpretation, and if the maces had pierced their heads before the boiling water was poured over them, then his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, Indeed, the boiling water penetrates the skull, would not have had any meaning. But the matter in that is contrary to what this speaker said. And his saying, It melts what is in their bellies and their skins, meaning: It melts with the boiling water that is poured over their heads what is in the fire: if you melt it, you melt it completely. And from this the poet says: I told him about a tree that was found in a desert, melted by the sun but not melted. And from it the saying of the rajaz poet: Grilled skewers doubt And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement it is melted with it, he said: it is melted completely. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Jurayj said, He melts with it: he said: He did not cut off their punishment. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly.
