Ibn Jurayj said, He melts with it: he said: He did not cut off their punishment. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them, to his statement, With it will melt what is in their bellies and their skins, meaning: They will be given to drink what, when it enters their bellies, melts them and their skins with the bellies. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far and Harun ibn `Antarah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr. Harun said: When the people of Hell are hungry, they will cry out to the tree of Zaqqum and eat from it, and the skin of their faces will be stripped off. If a passerby were to pass by them, he would recognize them, he would recognize the skin of their faces in it. Then thirst will be poured upon them, and they will cry out for help, and they will be given water like molten metal, the heat of which has reached its peak. When they bring it close to their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skin has fallen off, will be roasted by its heat. That which is in their bellies will be melted thereby, meaning their intestines, and their skin will fall off. Then they will be struck with iron mallets, and every limb will fall off as it was. They will cry out for woe and destruction. His statement, And for them will be mallets of iron, will be used by the guards to strike their heads with when they want to leave the Fire until they return to it. His statement, Every time they want to leave it, out of distress, they will be returned to it, means: every time. These infidels, whose description was given to them, were to be brought out of the Fire, from the grief and distress that befell them, and they were returned to it. Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ja`far ibn `Awn narrated to us, saying: Al-A`mash narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Thabyan, who said: The Fire is black and dark, and its flame and embers do not give light. Then he recited the verse: Every time they want to get out of it, they are returned to it. It was mentioned that they try to get out of the Fire when Hell is seething and throws those in it to the top of its gates. They want to get out, but the keepers throw them back into it with whips, and they say to them when they strike them with the whips: Taste the punishment of the burning. What he meant by his saying: Taste the punishment of the burning is that he says to them: Taste the punishment of the Fire. It was said: the punishment of the burning, and the meaning is: the burning, just as it was said: the painful punishment means: the painful.
22:20: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: It will melt what is in their bellies and their skins.
22:21: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And they will have maces of iron.
22:22: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Every time they want to get out of it, out of distress, they are returned to it and [they say], ‘Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire.’
22:23: God Almighty says: As for those who believed in God and His Messenger and obeyed them in what God commanded them to do of righteous deeds, God will admit them to Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow, and He will adorn them therein with bracelets of gold and pearls. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase and pearls. The scholars of the reciters of Medina and some of the people of Kufa read it in the accusative case with the one in the angels, meaning: they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls, in apposition to the pearls in the place of the bracelets, because the Mushaf is with the alif, so that is evidence of the correctness of the reading in the accusative case in it. The majority of the reciters of Iraq and Egypt read it as and pearls in the genitive case in apposition to the case of the pure bracelets. Those who read it also differed about the reason for proving the alif in it. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala, according to what was mentioned to me about him, said: It was proven in it as it was proven in qalu t and kulaw. Al-Kisa’i said: It was proven in it for the hamza, because the hamza is one of the letters. In my opinion, they are two well-known readings, each of which has been read by scholars of the Qur’an. They agree in meaning and are correct in their articulation in Arabic. So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And His statement, And their clothing therein will be silk, means: And their clothing that will touch their bodies therein will be silk garments. And His statement, And they will be guided to good speech, means, God Almighty says: And their Lord guided them in this world to the testimony that there is no god but God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, And they are guided to the good speech, he said: They are guided to the good speech: There is no god but God, God is greatest, and praise be to God. God said, To Him ascends the good speech, and the righteous deed raises it (Fatir 35:10). Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they are guided to the good word, he said: They were inspired. And His statement, And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy, God Almighty says. And their Lord guided them in this world to the path of the Praiseworthy Lord, and His path is His religion, the religion of Islam, which He legislated for His creation, and He commanded them to follow it. And the Praiseworthy is a verbal noun from the passive participle, and its meaning is that He is praised by His friends from among His creation, then He changed from praised to Praiseworthy.
22:24: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And they are guided to the good of speech and they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy.
22:25: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who have denied the Oneness of God, and have belied His Messengers, and have rejected what He has brought them from their Lord, and have turned people away from the path of God: He says: And they prevent people from entering the religion of God, and from the Sacred Mosque, which God has made for all the people who believe in Him, He has not specified some of it over others, the same for the one who is staying there and the one who is absent. He says: Moderate in what is required of him in terms of honoring the sanctity of the Sacred Mosque, and performing his rituals there, and staying there, wherever he wants, the one who is staying there, and the one who is absent: He is the one who returns to it from elsewhere. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said: Its meaning is: The one who is staying in it, who is residing in it, and the one who is absent are the same in that neither of them has more right to the home in it than the other. Who said that? Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said: Hakam narrated to us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Zaid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Ibn Sabit, he said: When the pilgrims came to Mecca, no one from the people of Mecca was more entitled to his home than them. When a man found plenty of space, he would stay, but theft spread among them, and each person would steal from his own side. So a man made a door, so Umar sent to him: Did you make a door for the pilgrims to the House of God? He said: No, I only made it to protect their belongings, and this is his saying: The one who stays there is the same as the one who passes by. He said: The one who passes by there is like the one who resides there. No one is more entitled to his home than anyone else, unless someone has reached a home before him. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, he said: I said to Saeed bin Jubair: Should I seclude myself in Mecca? He said: You are secluded, and he recited: The one who secludes himself therein and the one who comes by night are the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of someone who mentioned it, on the authority of Abu Salih: The one who is staying in it and the one who is absent are the same. The one who is staying in it is his family, and the one who is absent is the one who visits the house, they are the same. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, The one who stays therein and the one who passes by are the same, meaning: The people of Mecca and others will stay in the Sacred Mosque. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, The one who resides therein and the one who visits therein are the same, he said: The one who resides therein is the one who resides in Mecca, and the one who visits there is the one who comes to it, they are the same in the houses. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: It is the same for the one who is staying in it and the one who is absent. It is the same for his family and others. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The one who stays therein and the one who goes therein are the same, he said: The people of Mecca and others are the same in their dwellings. Others said something similar to what we said. Those who said this mentioned: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, The one who is staying therein is equal, he said: the one who is settled, and the one who is absent: the side, the right of God is equal upon them in it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The same applies to the one who is staying therein, he said: the resident, and the one who goes to the side, he said: the one who is absent. He said: Al-Husayn told us: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’, The one who is staying there is the same. They said: From his family, and the one who goes to him is the one who comes to him from outside his family. They are the same in his sanctity. We have chosen the statement we have chosen in this regard because God, the Most High, mentioned at the beginning of the verse that those who disbelieve in Him prevent those believers who want to perform their rituals in the Sacred Mosque from the Sacred Mosque, so He said, Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God and from the Sacred Mosque, then He, the Most High, mentioned the description of the Sacred Mosque, so He said, Which We have made for mankind, so He, the Most High, informed that He made it for all mankind, so the disbelievers in it prevent those believers who want it from it, then He said, The one who stays there and the one who visits there are equal, so it was known that His report about the equality of the one who stays there and the one who visits there is only in the meaning in which God began the report about the disbelievers, that they prevented the believers from it, and that is undoubtedly their circumambulation and performing their rituals there, and the place, not the report about their ownership of it and other than their ownership. And it was said, Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God, so He connected they avert and it is future to they disbelieved, and it is past, because averting means a description of them and permanence. If that is the meaning of the speech, it would only be in the form of a noun or the future tense and not in the form of the past. If that is the case, then the meaning of the speech is: Indeed, those who disbelieve are described as turning away from the path of God, and that is similar to the statement of God, Those who believe and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God (Al-Ra`d: 28). As for his statement, The one who is devoted to it is the same, then the reciters of the regions raise the one who is devoted to it with the one who is devoted to it, and the work we made in the attached ha’ and the lam that he says to the people, then he resumed the speech with the same, and the Arabs do the same when it comes after a letter that has been completed with it, so you say, I passed by a man who is equal to good and evil, the lowering may be permissible in that, but the raising is chosen in that because the same is in one school of thought among them, so it is as if they said: That is in the same, so he resumed with it, and he raised it and did not say it in moderate, because moderate is an explicit verb and the same is a source, so their taking it out to the verb is like their taking hasab in their statement, I passed by a man, enough for you from a man to the verb. It has been mentioned about some readers that he read it in the accusative case based on the action we made it in, and even though it has a face in Arabic, it is a reading that I do not permit reading with it due to the consensus of the proof from the readers to the contrary. And His statement, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice - We will make him taste a painful punishment, God Almighty says: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice - We will make him taste a painful punishment, which is that he inclines towards the Sacred House unjustly. And the letter ba’ was inserted in His statement, by an act of injustice, and the meaning is what I said, just as it was inserted in His statement, it grows oil, and the meaning is: it grows oil, as the poet said: In Wadi Yaman, the Shath grows at its top and bottom with Marakh and Shabhan. Meaning: Below it grow the marakh and the shabhan, as A’sha of Banu Tha’labah said: Our spears between the cauldrons and the pure white ones have guaranteed the livelihood of our children. Meaning: Our spears are guaranteed for our children’s sustenance. Some of the grammarians of Basra say so. As for some of the grammarians of Kufa, he used to say: The preposition ba was inserted in it, because its interpretation is: And whoever wants to commit injustice therein. And he used to say: The insertion of the preposition ba in an is easier than in ilhad and the like, because the prepositions are often omitted with it, and it is like a condition, so it is possible for the preposition to enter or leave, because the i’rab is not clear in it. And he said in the sources: The nominative and genitive are clear in it. He said: Abu al-Jarrah composed for me: When she did not drink, he shook the stick at her, stingy with her when she was about to give him a drink. And Imru Al-Qais said: Did he not come to her while the events were numerous, that Imru’ al-Qais ibn Malik was possessing a camel? He said: So he inserted the letter ba on the basis of an and it is in the nominative case, just as he inserted it on the basis of ilhad, which is in the accusative case. He said: And they inserted the letter ba on the basis of what they intended by it as a verbal noun, as the poet said: Didn't the report come to you about what happened to the camels of Banu Ziyad? He said: It is less than that in that it is less similar to the names than what. He said: I heard a Bedouin from Rabi’ah, and I asked him about something, and he said: I hope for that: he means I hope for that. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of the injustice that whoever wanted to commit an apostasy with it in the Sacred Mosque, God will make him taste painful torment, so some of them said: That is associating partners with God and worshipping other than Him with it: meaning with the House. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, he said: to commit polytheism. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, it means that he worships other than God therein. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, who said: And whoever intends to commit an act of injustice therein, he said: It is polytheism, and whoever commits polytheism in the House of God, God will punish him. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Others said: It is making permissible what is forbidden in it or riding it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And whoever intends therein to commit an injustice or wrongdoing - We will make him taste a painful punishment, means that you consider permissible what God has forbidden you, such as slander or murder, so you wrong someone who would not wrong you, and you kill someone who would not kill you, so if you do that, then a painful punishment is due to him. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, he said: He does a bad deed therein. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Kuraib and Nasr bin Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: There is no man who intends to commit a sin and it is recorded against him, and if a man, after he has made clear his intention to kill a man in this house, God will make him taste a painful torment. Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, Mujahid said, Yazid said, Shu’bah told us, he traced it back to the Prophet, and I will not trace it back to you in the statement of God, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice or wrongdoing - We will make him taste a painful punishment. He said: If a man intended to do evil therein while he was still in Abyan, God would make him taste a painful punishment. Al-Fadl bin Al-Sabah told us: Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, regarding his statement, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, he said: A man may intend to commit a sin in Mecca while he is in another country and does not know about it, and it is written down against him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice - We will make him taste a painful punishment, he said: Injustice is injustice in the sanctuary. Others said: Rather, the meaning of that injustice is: deliberately violating the sanctity. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: With injustice and wickedness he said: the one who wants to make it permissible deliberately. And it is said: polytheism. Others said: Rather, it is a food hoarding in Mecca. Who said that? Harun bin Idris Al-Asamm told me: Abd Al-Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, regarding his statement, And whoever intends therein to commit an injustice or wrong - We will make him taste a painful punishment, he said: They are the hoarders of food in Mecca. Others said: Rather, that is everything that was forbidden from knowledge, even the saying of the one who says: No, by God, and yes, by God. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn `Amr, he said: He had two tents: one outside the sacred precincts and the other inside the sacred precincts. When he wanted to reproach his family, he would reproach them outside the sacred precincts. He was asked about that, and he said: We used to say that it was an act of heresy for a man to say: No, by God, and yes, by God. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Abu Rabi’ah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: Abdullah bin Amr used to say: No, by God, and indeed, from the heresy in it. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the statements we have mentioned in interpreting this is the statement we have mentioned from Ibn Mas`ud and Ibn `Abbas, that what is meant by injustice in this place is every disobedience to God. This is because God has made it general in His statement, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, and has not specified one act of injustice over another in any report or intellect, so it is general. If this is the case, then the interpretation of the statement is: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, disobeying God therein, We will make him taste, on the Day of Resurrection, a painful punishment. It has been mentioned from some of the reciters that he used to recite this, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, disobeying God therein, We will make him taste, on the Day of Resurrection, a painful punishment. It has been mentioned from some of the reciters that he used to recite it, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, from the place, I will return him. This is a reading that I do not allow to be recited with, because it contradicts what the evidence of the reciters agree upon, and because it is far from the eloquent speech of the Arabs. This is because to return is an action that occurs, and it is said from it: He is returning to such and such a place or town tomorrow, but it is not said: He is returning to such and such a place. Some people who know the Arabic language have claimed that Tayy’ tribe says: I desired you, meaning: I desired you. It was mentioned that some of them recited a verse to him: I prefer to be with Laqit and his gang, but I do not prefer Sinbas. Meaning: And I desire it. If that is correct as we mentioned, then it is permissible in speech. As for reading it, it is not permissible for what I described.
22:26: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his teacher of the greatness of what the people of Quraysh have done in particular, without others from all of His creation, by worshipping Him in His sanctuary, and the House that He ordered His friend Abraham, may God bless him and grant him peace, to build and purify from plagues, doubt and polytheism: And remember, O Muhammad, how We began this House in which your people worship other than Me, when We provided for Our friend Abraham, meaning by His saying: provided: and We paved the place of the House for him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, he said: God established the House after Adam, peace be upon him, when Adam was sent down to earth, and his place of descent was in the land of India. His head was in the sky and his feet were on the earth, so the angels feared him and they would come down to sixty cubits. When Adam lost the angels’ voices and their glorification, he complained about that to God, so God said: O Adam, I have sent down to you a House that is circumambulated as one circumambulates around My Throne, so go to it, and God came out and extended his steps for him, so that between every two steps there was a wilderness, and those wildernesses remained like that until Adam came to the House, so he circumambulated it, and after him the prophets. Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: When God commanded Abraham and Ishmael to purify My House for those who perform Tawaf, Abraham set out until he came to Mecca, and he and Ishmael stood up, and took pickaxes, not knowing where the House was. Then God sent a wind called the wind of Al-Khajuj, which had two wings and a head in the form of a snake, and it swept for them what was around the Kaaba from the foundation of the first House, and they followed it with pickaxes, digging, until the foundation. That is when He says, And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House and by the House he means the Kaaba, that you associate nothing with Me in your worship of Me and purify My House which you had built from the worship of idols. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, regarding his statement, And purify my house, he said: from polytheism. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair, he said: From the plagues and doubt. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Purify my house, he said: from polytheism and the worship of idols. His saying, for those who circumambulate it, means for those who circumambulate it, and those who stand means those who pray and are standing in their prayers. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement, And purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stand up, he said: Those who stand up in prayer. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, and the standing ones: he said: the standing ones are the praying ones. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And those who stand, bow, and prostrate, he said: The one who stands, bows, and prostrates is the one who prays, and the one who circumambulates it is the one who circumambulates it. And His statement, And those who bow and prostrate, he said: And those who bow and prostrate in their prayer around the House.
22:27: God the Almighty says: We also charged him to proclaim the Hajj to the al-Nas 114:He means by His saying and proclaim inform and call to the people that you people should perform Hajj to the Sacred House of God. They will come to you on foot He says: for the people will come to the House that you command them to perform Hajj on foot, and on every lean camel He says: and riding on every lean camel, and they are the thin camels. They will come from every distant pass He says: they will come, so it was made plural because what was meant by every lean camel is the female camels. The meaning of all is the plural, so that is why it was said: they will come. Al-Farra’ claimed that it is rare in the speech of the Arabs: I passed by every man standing. He said: And this is correct, and God’s saying and on every lean camel they will come indicates the validity of its permissibility. It was mentioned that when God commanded Abraham, peace be upon him, to call for Hajj, he stood at his place and called out: O people, God has prescribed Hajj for you, so perform Hajj to His ancient House. There is disagreement about the manner in which Abraham was harmed by that. Some of them said: He called for that as: Ibn Humayd told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When Abraham finished building the House, it was said to him, Proclaim the Hajj to the people. He said, O Lord, how can my voice reach? He said, Proclaim, and I am responsible for conveying it. Then Abraham called out, O people, Hajj to the Ancient House has been prescribed for you, so perform Hajj. He said, “And everything between the heaven and the earth heard him. Do you not see the people coming from the farthest ends of the earth, all adorned with garments of clothing?” Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Muhammad bin Fadil bin Ghazwan Al-Dhabi told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When Abraham built the House, God revealed to him to call people to perform Hajj. He said: Abraham said: Behold, your Lord has built a House and has commanded you to perform Hajj to it. So whatever he heard of stone, tree, hill, dirt, or anything else responded to him: Here I am, O God, here I am. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya ibn Wadh told us: Ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And proclaim to the people the Hajj, he said: Abraham, the friend of God, stood on the Black Stone and called: O people, Hajj has been prescribed for you, so those in the loins of men and the wombs of women heard, and those who believed and who had been predestined by God to perform Hajj until the Day of Resurrection responded: Here I am, O God, here I am. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, “And proclaim to the people the Hajj. They will come to you on foot,” he said: And it was established in the heart of every male and female. Ibn Hamid told me: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: When Abraham finished building the House, God revealed to him, Proclaim the Hajj to the people. He said: So he went out and called out to the al-Nas 114:O people, your Lord has built a House, so perform the Hajj to it. On that day, no human, jinn, tree, hill, soil, mountain, water, or anything else heard him except that he said: At your service, O God, at your service. He said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And proclaim to the people the Hajj, he said: Abraham stood at his station and said: O people, respond to your Lord. They said: Here I am, O God, here I am. So whoever performs Hajj today is among those who responded to Abraham on that day. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah bin Khalid Al-Makhzumi, who said: When Abraham, peace be upon him, finished building the House, he stood on the station and called out a call that the people of the earth heard: Your Lord has built for you a House, so perform Hajj to it. Dawud said: I hope that whoever performs Hajj today will answer Abraham, peace be upon him. Muhammad bin Sinan al-Qazzaz told me: Hajjaj told us: Hammad told us, on the authority of Abu Asim al-Ghanawi, on the authority of Abu al-Tayfil, who said: Ibn Abbas said: Do you know how the Talbiyah was? I said: How was the Talbiyah? He said: When Abraham was commanded to call the people to Hajj, the mountains were lowered for him into a plain, and the towns were raised, so he called the people to prayer. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And proclaim to the people the Hajj, Ibrahim said: How do I say, O Lord? He said: Say: O people, respond to your Lord. He said: And it is established in the heart of every believer. And others said about that, what: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: It was said to Ibrahim, Proclaim the Hajj to the people. He said: O Lord, what should I say? He said: Say, ‘Here I am, O God, here I am.’ He said: And that was the first Talbiyah. Ibn Abbas used to say: What is meant by people in this place are the people of the Qiblah. The novel mentioned that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And proclaim to the people the Hajj, meaning by the al-Nas 114:the people of the Qiblah. Have you not heard that he said, Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Makkah - blessed (Al Imran 3:96)... to his statement, And whoever enters it shall be safe (Al Imran 3:97) meaning: And whoever enters it from among the people among whom the call to prayer was commanded, and upon whom the Hajj was prescribed, then he shall be safe, so magnify the sanctities of God Almighty, for that is from the piety of the hearts. As for his saying, They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: They come to you on foot, he said: On foot. He said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Arta’ah, he said: Ibn Abbas said: I do not regret anything that I missed, except that I performed Hajj on foot, I heard God say, They will come to you on foot. He said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Abraham and Ishmael performed Hajj on foot. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They come to you on foot, he said: On their feet. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And on every lean animal, he said: camels. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: And on every lean animal, he said: camels. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me, he said: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Omar bin Dhir, he said: Mujahid said: They did not ride, so God revealed: They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel. He said: So he ordered them to take provisions, and gave them permission to ride and trade. And his saying: From every deep valley. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, from every deep valley meaning: from a distant place. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: From every deep valley. He said: Far away. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, A deep valley he said: A distant place. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. And His saying, That they may witness benefits for themselves. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the benefits that God mentioned in this place. Some of them said: They are trade and worldly benefits. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, he said: Amr told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, That they may witness benefits for themselves. He said: They are the markets. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir bin Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Trade. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdala, on the authority of Abu Razin, regarding his statement, that they may witness benefits for themselves, he said: their markets. He said: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Waqid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: So that they may witness benefits for themselves. He said: Trade. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Waqid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the same. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Waqid, on the authority of Saeed, the same. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Sinan told us, on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, on the authority of Abu Razin, So that they may witness benefits for themselves, he said: the markets. Others said: It is the reward in the afterlife, and trade in this world. Who said that? Ibn Bashar and Suwar bin Abdullah told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: That they may witness benefits for themselves. He said: Trade, and what pleases God of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us: Sufyan told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, that they may witness benefits for themselves, he said: the reward in the Hereafter, and trade in this world. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, Warqa’ both said, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Others said: Rather, it is forgiveness and pardon. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, So that they may witness benefits for themselves. He said: Pardon. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, he said: Muhammad bin Ali said: Forgiveness. The most correct of the sayings is the saying of the one who said: He meant by that: So that they may witness benefits for themselves from the work that pleases God and from trade, and that is because God has made general for them the benefits of all that the season witnesses, and that which comes to Mecca during the days of the season from the benefits of this world and the hereafter, and He did not specify any of that from their benefits by report or reason, so that is in general for the benefits that were described. And His statement, And that they may mention the name of God on known days over what He has provided for them of sacrificial animals, God Almighty says: And that they may mention the name of God over what He has provided for them of gifts and sacrificial animals which they have presented of camels, cows and sheep, on known days, and they are the days of Tashreeq according to some of the people of interpretation. And according to some of them, the ten days. And according to some of them, the Day of Sacrifice and the days of Tashreeq. We have mentioned the differences of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding this in the narrations. We have explained the first and most correct of them in Surat Al-Baqarah, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. However, I will also mention some of that in this place. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And let them mention the name of God on known days, meaning the days of Tashreeq. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement, On known days, meaning the days of Tashreeq, On what He has provided for them of livestock, meaning the sacrificial animals. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, On known days. He said: The ten days, and the numbered days: The days of Tashreeq. And His saying, Then eat from it, means: Eat from the livestock over which you mentioned the name of God, O people, there. And this command from God, may He be glorified, is a command of permission, not a command of obligation. That is because there is no disagreement among all the jurists that the one who slaughters his sacrificial animal or camel there, if he does not eat from his sacrificial animal, has not wasted an obligation that was obligatory upon him, so it is known from that that it is not obligatory. Mentioning the narration of some of the scholars who said that: Suwar bin Abdullah told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement, So eat from it and feed the poor and needy. He said: He did not consider eating from it to be obligatory. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: It is a concession: if he wants, he may eat, and if he wants, he may not eat. It is like His saying: And when you are in ihram, then hunt (al-Ma’idah 5:2), And when the prayer is concluded, then disperse within the land (al-Jumuah 62:10), meaning His saying: So eat from it and feed the contented and the needy (al-Hajj 22:36). He said: Hisham told us, he said: Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, So eat from it, he said: It is a concession: if he wants to eat, he may eat, and if he wants to not eat, he may not eat. He said: Hisham told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement, So eat from it, he said: It is a concession, so if he wants to eat it, he may eat it, and if he wants to, he may not eat it. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Zaid told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So eat from it, he said: It is only a concession. And His statement, And feed the wretched and needy, means: And feed from what you slaughter or sacrifice there of the livestock, from your offerings and your bodies, the wretched, who is the one who is afflicted by hunger, hardship, and need. The poor: the one who has nothing. And in a similar manner to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, So eat from it and feed the poor and needy, meaning: the poor and needy. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid: The wretched, the needy is the one who extends his hand to you. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, the wretched, the needy, he said: He is the contented. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Umar ibn Ata’ told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: The wretched is the one who is in need and is afflicted with misery, and the poor is the one who is self-sufficient. He said: Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, the wretched one is the one who stretches out his hands. And his statement, Then let them complete their rites, God Almighty says: Then let them complete what is required of them of the rites of their Hajj: shaving their hair, trimming their moustache, throwing pebbles, and circumambulating the House. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Al-Ash’ath bin Suwar told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that he said: Then let them complete their ritual purity. He said: What they are doing during Hajj. Humayd bin Mas`adah told us: Yazid told us: Al-Ash`ath told us, on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of Ibn `Umar, who said: Al-Tafth means all the rituals. He said: Hisham told us, he said: Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said, regarding His statement, Then let them complete their ceremonial ceremonies, he said: Ceremonial ceremonies include shaving the head, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, cutting the nails, trimming the sideburns, throwing stones, and standing at Arafat and Muzdalifah. Hamid told us, he said: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Khalid told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Tuffath: hair and nails. Yaqoub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, that he used to say regarding this verse, Then let them complete their rites,: throwing the pebbles, slaughtering the animal, trimming the moustache, beard and nails, and circumambulating the House and Safa and Marwa. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said regarding this verse, Then let them complete their rites of celibacy. He said: It is shaving the head. And he mentioned some things about the Hajj, and Shu`bah said: I do not remember them. He said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Then let them complete their rites of celibacy, he said: shaving the head, shaving the pubic hair, trimming the nails, trimming the moustache, throwing the pebbles, and trimming the beard. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Except that he did not say in his hadith: and trimming the beard. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me, he said: Al-Maharibi told us, he said: I heard a man asking Ibn Jurayj about his statement, Then let them complete their rites. He said: Trimming the beard and moustache, trimming the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, and throwing the pebbles. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Mansour told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, and Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, that they both said: Shaving the head. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Then let them complete their rites, meaning: shaving the head. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Shaving the head and trimming the nails. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then let them complete their rituals, meaning: their rituals. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then let them complete their rites, he said: The rites are their ihram. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then let them complete their ritual purity. He said: By ritual purity, he meant removing their ritual purity from shaving the head, putting on clothes, cutting the nails, and the like. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, who said: Shaving the hair, trimming the nails, trimming the moustache, shaving the pubic hair, and all of the Hajj rituals. His saying, And let them fulfill their vows, means: And let them fulfill to God what they vowed of offerings, sacrificial animals, and other things. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And let them fulfill their vows, is to slaughter the sacrificial animals that they vowed. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us - and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And let them fulfill their vows the vow of Hajj and the sacrifice, and whatever a person vows of something that is during Hajj. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, And let them fulfill their vows. He said: The vow of Hajj and the sacrifice, and whatever a person vows to himself of something that is during Hajj. And his saying, And let them circumambulate the Ancient House, means: And let them circumambulate the Sacred House of God. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his saying the ancient in this place. Some of them said: This was said about the Sacred House of God, because God freed it from the tyrants so that they would not reach the point of destroying and demolishing it. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, that Ibn al-Zubayr said: It was called the Ancient House because God freed it from the tyrants. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: He was called Al-Ateeq because he was freed from the tyrants. He said: Sufyan told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada: And to go around the Ancient House. He said: Free from the tyrants. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, the ancient house, he said: God freed it from the tyrants, meaning the Kaaba. Others said: It was called Ateeq because no one owned it. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ubaid, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The House was called the Ancient House because no one had anything in it. Others said: It was named thus because of its age. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement: The ancient house. He said: The ancient is the old, because it is old, just as it is said: the ancient sword, because it was the first house established for people. Adam built it, and he was the first to build it, then God designated its place for Abraham after the drowning, so Abraham and Ishmael built it. Abu Ja`far said: All of these statements that we mentioned from those we mentioned about his saying, the ancient house, have a correct aspect, except that what Ibn Zayd said is most likely to be correct in its meanings on the surface, except that what was narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr is more correct, if it is what: Muhammad bin Sahl al-Bukhari told me: Abdullah bin Saleh told us: Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Khalid bin Musfir, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Muhammad bin Urwah, on the authority of Abdullah bin al-Zubayr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Ancient House was named so because God freed it from the tyrants, so they never prevailed over it. Sahih. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Al-Zuhri said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It was only called the Ancient House because God freed it. Then he mentioned something similar. What is meant by the circumambulation that God Almighty commanded the pilgrim to His ancient house to do in this verse is the circumambulation of farewell, which is done after the declaration, either on the Day of Sacrifice or after it. There is no disagreement among the people of interpretation about that. Mentioning the narration of some of those who said that: Amr bin Saeed Al-Qurashi told us: Al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And let them circumambulate the Ancient House. He said: The circumambulation of visitation. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Khalid told us, he said: Al-Ash’ath told us, that Al-Hasan said regarding his statement, And to perform Tawaf around the Ancient House, meaning: for the obligatory Tawaf. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And to go around the Ancient House, meaning: to visit the House. Yaqoub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hajjaj and Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement, And to circumambulate the Ancient House, he said: Circumambulating on the Day of Sacrifice. Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Barqi told me: Amr bin Abi Salamah told us: I asked Zuhair about the words of God: And let them go around the Ancient House. He said: The farewell circumambulation. The reciters differed in the reading of these letters. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as Then let them complete their untidiness and fulfill their vows and let them circumambulate with a sukoon on the lam in all of that in order to make it easier, as they did in He if it was preceded by a waw, so they said He is All-Knowing of the Iron-bound: 6, so they sukooned the ha’. They do the same with the lam of the imperative if it is preceded by letters from the letters of the sequence such as the waw, the fa’, and thumma. The majority of the reciters of Basra read it as such, except that Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ used to break the lam in his saying Then let them complete their untidiness specifically because stopping at Then rather than Liyaqdha is good, and stopping at the waw and the fa’ is not permissible. This is what Abu Amr relied on because his reading of it is good from the point of view of analogy, except that most of the reciters keep it sukoon. The first of the correct sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is that the sukoon on the lam of li-yaqdhu and the kasra are two well-known readings and two common languages, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct, except that the kasra in it is more correct, for what we mentioned to Abu Amr about the reason, because whoever reads And He is All-Knowing of that which is in the breasts (al-Hadid 57:6) then he sukoon the ha’ with the waw and the fa’, and he moves it in his statement Then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth (al-Qasas 28:61). So that is what he must do in his statement Then let them complete their untidiness so he moves the lam to the kasra with thumma, even if he sukoon it in his statement And let them fulfill their vows and it has been mentioned from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Hasan al-Basri that it is moved with thumma and the waw, and it is a well-known language, except that most of the readers with the waw and the fa’ with it being sukoon, it is the most well-known of the two languages in the Arabs and the most eloquent, so reading with it is more pleasing to me than its kasra.
22:28: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of God on known days over what He has provided for them of livestock. So eat from them and feed the poor and needy.”
22:29: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Then let them complete their untidiness and fulfill their vows and perform Tawaf around the Ancient House.
22:30: God Almighty means by His saying that: This which He has commanded of performing the ritual purification, fulfilling vows, and circumambulating the Ancient House is the obligation that is incumbent upon you, O people, during your Hajj. And whoever honors the sacred limits of God, it is better for him with his Lord. He says: And whoever avoids what God has commanded him to avoid during his state of ihram, out of his honoring the limits of God that he should not violate them and His sacred limits that he should not consider permissible, it is better for him with his Lord in the Hereafter. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said, regarding his statement, “That is so. And whoever honors the sacred ordinances of God,” he said: Mecca, the Hajj and Umrah, and all of the sins that God has forbidden. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And whoever honors the sacred ordinances of God, he said: The sacred ordinances are: the Sacred Monument, the Sacred House, the Sacred Mosque, and the Sacred City. These are the sacred ordinances. And His statement, And the livestock have been made lawful to you, God Almighty says: God has made lawful to you, O people, the livestock, that you may eat them if you slaughter them. He has not forbidden you from them the bahīrah, nor the Ṣa’ibah, nor the wasīlah, nor the Ḥamī, nor what you have made of them for your gods, except what is recited to you, meaning: except what is recited to you in the Book of God, and that is: dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God, and that which has been strangled, and that which has been beaten to death, and that which has fallen from its neck, and that which has been gored, and that which has been eaten by a wild beast, and that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, for all of that is impure. As Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Except what is recited to you, he said: Except for dead meat, and that over which the name of God has not been mentioned. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. His saying, So avoid the uncleanliness of idols, means: So avoid the worship of idols and obeying Satan in worshipping them, for they are unclean. And in a similar manner to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, So avoid the uncleanness of idols, God Almighty says: So avoid obeying Satan in worshipping idols. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, The abomination of idols, he said: The worship of idols. And His statement, And avoid false statement, God Almighty says: And beware of false statement and falsehood against God by your statement about the gods, We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to God (al-Zumar 39:3), and your statement about the angels, They are the daughters of God, and similar statements, for that is a lie and falsehood, and polytheism with God. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: false speech, he said: lying. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And avoid false statement, being true to God, not associating anything with Him. Meaning: slandering God and lying. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Wa’il bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: False testimony is equal to polytheism, and he recited: So avoid the uncleanness of idols and avoid false statement. Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Wa’il ibn Rabi’ah, who said: False testimony is equal to polytheism. Then he recited this verse: So avoid the uncleanness of idols and avoid false statement. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Abu Usama told us, he said: Sufyan Al-Asfari told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Khuraim bin Fatik, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: False testimony is equal to associating partners with God. Then he recited: So avoid the uncleanness of idols and avoid false statement. Abu Kuraib narrated: Marwan bin Muawiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Asfari, on the authority of Fatik bin Fadala, on the authority of Ayman bin Khuraim, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to deliver a sermon and said: O people, false testimony is equal to associating partners with God, twice. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘So avoid the uncleanness of idols and avoid false statement.’” It is possible that what was meant by this was: O people, avoid becoming unclean of idols by worshipping them. If someone were to say: Are there idols that are not unclean, so that it was said: So avoid the uncleanness among them? It would be said: All of them are unclean, and the meaning is not what you have gone to in that. Rather, the meaning of the statement is: So avoid the uncleanness that comes from idols, that is, worshipping them. What God, the Most High, commanded with His saying: So avoid the uncleanness from them is to avoid worshipping them, and that worship is uncleanness according to what Ibn Abbas said, and what we mentioned before.
22:31: God the Almighty says: O people, avoid the worship of idols and the saying of polytheism, being upright for God in sincere monotheism for Him, and singling out obedience and worship for Him alone without idols and statues, not associating anything with Him besides Him, for whoever associates anything with God besides Him, then his example in his distance from guidance and attaining the truth and his destruction and his departure from his Lord is like someone who falls from the sky, and the birds snatch him up and he perishes, or the wind blows with him and crushes him. From this, the tall palm tree is called the palm tree of Sahuq, and from this is the saying of the poet: We had a neighbor who was bothered by filth that deserved to be thrown away. He narrates: You deserve it. He says: Thus is the example of the polytheist in his distance from his Lord, and from attaining the truth, like the distance of this reality from the sky to the earth, or like the destruction of one of them who was snatched by a bird in the air. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: As if he had fallen from the sky. He said: This is a parable that God gave for those who associate partners with God in their distance from guidance and their destruction. Then the birds snatch him away or the wind hurls him into a remote place. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, in a distant place, he said: far away. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. It was said, Then the birds snatched him away, and it was said before that, As if he had fallen from the sky. “Fall” is a past tense verb, and snatched away is a future tense verb, so the future was connected to the past, as He did in the phrase, Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God (al-Hajj 22:25), and I explained that there.
22:32: God Almighty says: This is what I have mentioned to you, O people, and commanded you to do, of avoiding the filth of idols, and avoiding false speech, being upright for God, and venerating the symbols of God, which is improving the body and making it fat, and performing the rituals of Hajj, as God Almighty has commanded, from the piety of your hearts. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, he said: Muhammad bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And whoever honors the symbols of God - indeed, it is from the piety of hearts, he said: Honoring them, appreciating them, and considering them good. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And whoever honors the symbols of God, he said: To be proud and to be great. And on his authority, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same, except that he said: and approval. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Wasiti told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, and Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And whoever venerates the symbols of God, he said: venerating the body, considering it fat, and appreciating it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Yazid ibn Harun told us: Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, who said: Standing at Arafat is one of the rites of God, and gathering is one of the rites of God, and throwing the pebbles is one of the rites of God, and the sacrificial animals are one of the rites of God, and whoever honors them, then they are one of the rites of God in His statement: And whoever honors the rites of God, so whoever honors them, then they are from the piety of the heart. Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And whoever honors the symbols of God, he said: The symbols are the Jamarat, and Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of God, and Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, and Muzdalifah. He said: The symbols are included in the sanctuary, they are symbols and they are the sanctuary. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty mentioned that the glorification of His symbols, which are what He made signs for His creation in what He worshipped them with from the rituals of their Hajj, from the places that He commanded them to perform what He imposed upon them from them, and the actions that He obligated them to do in their Hajj: is from the piety of their hearts. He did not specify anything from that, so the glorification of all of that is from the piety of the hearts, as He, the Most High, said: And it is right for His believing servants to glorify all of that, and He said: For it is from the piety of the hearts, and He made it feminine and did not say: for it, because that is what was meant by that, for that glorification along with avoiding the uncleanness of the idols is from the piety of the hearts, as He, the Most High, said: Indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful (al-A’raf 7:153). And what He meant by His saying: For it is from the piety of the hearts is that it is from the trembling of the hearts from the fear of God, and the truth of their knowledge of His greatness and the sincerity of His monotheism.
22:33: People differed about the meaning of the benefits that God mentioned in this verse, and informed His servants that they are for a specified term, in the same way that they differed about the meaning of the rituals that He, the Most High, mentioned in His saying, And whoever honors the symbols of God - indeed, it is from the piety of the hearts. Those who said that the rituals are the bodies, meaning: You, O people, have benefits in the bodies. Then those who said this statement also differed about the state in which they have benefits, and the term in which He, the Most High, said, for a specified term. Some of them said: The state in which God, the Most High, informed them that they have benefits, is the state in which its owner did not make it obligatory, nor did He call it a camel, nor did He put it on a mount. They said: Its benefits in this state are: drinking its milk, riding its backs, and what God provides them from its offspring and children. They said: The appointed term that God Almighty has informed us is for His believing servants from Him to Him, is until they make it obligatory for them. So if they make it obligatory, that becomes void, and they will have nothing of it. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding Therein you have benefits for a specified term, he said: As long as no physical body is specified. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us: Ishaq bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Therein you have benefits for a specified term, he said: The cup, the milk, and the child. If you name a camel or a gift, it is all gone. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding this verse, You have benefits in them for a specified term, he said: You have in their backs, their milk, and their hair, until they become a camel. He said: Ibn Adi told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, and Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: For you therein are benefits for a specified term. He said: In its hair, fur, and milk, before you call it a sacrificial animal. He said: Harun bin Al-Mughira narrated to us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Therein you have benefits for a specified term, he said: In the body, its meat, milk, hair, fur, and wool before it is designated as an offering. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly, and he added to it: And it is the appointed term. Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj informed us, on the authority of Ata’, that he said regarding His statement, “There are benefits for you in them for a specified term. Then their place of residence is at the Ancient House,” he said: Benefits in their milk, their backs, and their hair, for a specified term: until they are put on yoke. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah said: I heard Ibn Abi Nujayh say regarding His statement, Therein you have benefits for a specified term, he said: Until a camel makes it obligatory. He said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Qatada: Therein you have benefits for a specified term. He said: In their backs and their milk. So if they are hung up, their place is at the Ancient House. Others said: The rituals are the animals in His statement, And whoever honors the symbols of God - indeed, it is from the piety of the hearts. The ha in His statement, for you therein is from the mention of the rituals, and the meaning of His statement, for you therein are benefits is that you have benefits in the rituals that you honor for God after you have taken them as animals or sacrifices for God, by riding on their backs if you need to do so, and drinking their milk if you are forced to boil them. They said: And the appointed term that God, the Most High, said, for a appointed term is until it is slaughtered. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’: Therein you have benefits for a specified term. He said: It is riding the camel and drinking its milk if needed. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said regarding his statement, Therein you have benefits for a specified term, he said: Until it is slaughtered. He told him that the one who is exhausted or who is cut off from his family due to necessity should carry it on it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would command that if its master needed a sacrificial animal, he should carry it on it and ride it when he was in need of it. Exhausted. I said to Ata’: What? He said: The man on foot, and the one who is cut off from it, and the one who follows it, even if it gives birth, that he carries her offspring on it, and he does not drink from her milk except what is left over from her offspring, and if there is excess in her milk then let him who gave her as a gift drink and whoever did not give her as a gift drink. As for those who said: The meaning of the rituals in His statement, And whoever honors the symbols of God: the rituals of Hajj, which are the places where the sacrifices are performed for God, then they also differed regarding the meaning of the benefits of which God said, Therein are benefits for you. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: In these rituals that you honor, you have benefits through your trade there, and your buying and selling in its presence and your marketing. And the appointed term: leaving the rituals to others, and from the places where the sacrifices are performed to what is other than them according to the statement of some of them. Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me: Abu Osama told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Dhabi, on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, on the authority of Abi Razin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Therein are benefits for you, he said: Their markets, for he did not mention benefits except for the world. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Yazid bin Harun told us, he said: Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Musa, his statement, Therein you have benefits for a specified term, he said: The specified term is the exit from it to another. Others among them said: The benefits that God mentioned in this place: working for God with what He commanded of the Hajj rituals. They said: And the appointed term: is the expiration of the days of Hajj in which one performs the Hajj ritual for God. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, “For you therein are benefits for a specified term. Then their place of return is at the Ancient House,” he recited the statement of God, And whoever honors the symbols of God - indeed, it is from the piety of hearts. For you therein are benefits for a specified term. When those days pass, you will not see anyone coming to Arafat and standing there, seeking reward, nor to Muzdalifah, nor to throw the pebbles. They have identified countries for these days in which there are benefits, but their benefits are only for those days, which are the specified term, then their place of return when those days pass is at the Ancient House. Abu Ja`far said: We have already demonstrated that the statement of God, the Most High, And whoever honors the symbols of God, means: everything that was of work or place that God made a sign for the rituals of Hajj of His creation, since He, the Most High, did not specify anything of that in a report or intellect. Since that is the case, it is known that the meaning of His statement, For you therein are benefits for a specified term, in these symbols are benefits for a specified term. So whatever of these symbols were animals and offerings, their benefits are for you from the time you own them until you make them obligatory as gifts and animals. Whatever of them were places where rituals are performed for God, their benefits are trade for God there, and doing what He commanded until departing from them.
