Whatever of them were times where God is obeyed by doing the works of Hajj and seeking a livelihood in them through trade, until one circumambulates the House in some cases, or reaches the Sacred Sanctuary in some cases, and leaves the Sacred Sanctuary in some cases. Those we mentioned differed in their interpretation of His statement, Therein you have benefits for a specified term, in their interpretation of His statement, Then its destination is the Ancient House. Those who said: What is meant by the rituals in this place is the body, meaning that then the destination of the body is until it reaches Mecca, which is where the Ancient House is. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’, Then its place of residence is at the Ancient House, to Mecca. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House, meaning the place of sacrifice when it is called to the Ancient House. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Then its place when it is called a gift to the Ancient House, he said: The Kaaba is the most emancipated of the tyrants. So these people directed the interpretation of that to then the place of slaughtering the sacrificial animals and the gifts that you have made obligatory to the land of the Sacred Sanctuary, and they said: What is meant by the Ancient House is the entire land of the Sacred Sanctuary, and they said: That is similar to His statement: So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque (al-Tawbah 9:28), and what is meant is: the entire Sacred Sanctuary. Others said: The meaning of this is: Then your place, O people, in the rituals of your pilgrimage to the Ancient House is to circumambulate it on the Day of Sacrifice, after you have completed what God has obligated upon you in your pilgrimage. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Yazid bin Harun told us: Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Musa: Then its place is at the Ancient House. He said: The place of all these rituals is: circumambulating the House. Others said: The meaning of this is: Then the place of the benefits of the days of Hajj to the Ancient House ends with their expiration. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House, when those days, the days of the pilgrimage to the Ancient House, have passed. The first of these sayings, in my opinion, to be correct is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: Then the place of the rituals in which you have benefits for a specified period is the Ancient House. So whatever of that is a sacrifice or an animal, then it is by meeting it in the sanctuary in the sanctuary, and whatever of it is a ritual, then it is circumambulating the House. We have explained the correct meaning of what we say about rituals.
22:34: God Almighty says, And for every nation and for every group of people who have a predecessor among you from the people of faith in God, O people, We have made a sacrifice whose blood they shed that they may mention the name of God over what He has provided for them of grazing livestock with that, because among the animals are those that are not grazing livestock, such as horses, mules, and donkeys. It was said: The reason why the animals are called grazing animals is because they speak. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement, We made a ritual, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And for every nation We have appointed rites he said: the shedding of blood that they may mention the name of God over what Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. And His statement, Your God is one God, the Most High says: So avoid the uncleanliness of idols, and avoid false speech, for your God is one God, with no partner for Him, so worship Him, and devote your divinity to Him. And His statement, Then submit to Him, means: So submit to your God in obedience, and humble yourself to Him in acknowledging servitude. And His statement, And give good tidings to the humble, the Most High says: And give good tidings, O Muhammad, to those who submit to God in obedience, who surrender to Him in servitude, and who turn to Him in repentance. We have explained the meaning of humility with its evidence in what has preceded in this book of ours. The interpreters differed about what is meant by it in this place. Some of them said: What is meant by it is: And give good tidings to those who are reassured by God. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And give good tidings to the humble. He said: the reassured. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And give good tidings to the humble, those who are reassured by God. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us. And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And give good tidings to the humble, he said: the reassured. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And give good tidings to the humble, he said: the humble. Others said about this: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abd God ibn Aws, on the authority of Amr ibn Aws, who said: The humble ones are those who are not wronged, and if they are wronged, they do not seek revenge. Muhammad bin Othman Al-Wasiti told me: Hafs bin Omar told us: Muhammad bin Muslim Al-Ta’ifi told us: Othman bin Abdullah bin Aws told me, on the authority of Amr bin Aws, the same.
22:35: This is one of the descriptions of the humble. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And give good tidings, O Muhammad, to the humble whose hearts are humble at the remembrance of God, and are submissive out of fear of Him and fear of His punishment, and fear of His wrath. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Those whose hearts become fearful when God is mentioned, he said: Their hearts do not harden. And those who are patient over what befalls them of hardship in the matter of God, and what befalls them of hardship in His side. “And those who establish the obligatory prayer. “And from what We have provided them” of wealth, they spend in what is obligatory upon them to spend in zakat, and the maintenance of their children, and those whose maintenance is obligatory upon them, and in the way of God.
22:36: God Almighty says: And the body: which is the plural of badana, and its singular may be called badan. And if it is said badan, it could be a plural and a singular, and it is indicated that it could be said that for a singular by the saying of the rajaz poet: When you have control over things, you must fast for months and make vows. My head was shaved and braided, and my body was well-armored and well-groomed. Al-Badan: is the largest of everything, and for this reason it was said to Imru’ al-Qais ibn al-Nu’man, the owner of al-Khawranq and al-Sudair: Al-Badan: for his largeness and the looseness of his flesh, as it is said: He has become fat and we have shown him. So the meaning of the speech and the camels are the great bodies and huge bodies, we have made them for you, O people, from the symbols of God: He says: From the signs of the command of God that He commanded you with in the rituals of your Hajj, if you put them on and covered them and marked them, it is known of that, and it is felt that you did that from the camels and cows. As Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata’ said: And the sacrificial animals We have made for you among the rites of God, he said: The cow and the camel. And his saying, There is good for you in it, means that there is good for you in the body, and that good is the reward in the Hereafter for slaughtering it and giving it in charity, and in this world: riding if he needs to ride it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Therein is good for you, he said: Reward and benefits for the body. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, There is good for you in it. He said: Milk and riding if you need it. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim: There is good for you in it. He said: If you are forced to ride your sacrificial animal, ride it and drink its milk. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: There is good for you in it. Whoever needs the back of a sacrificial animal may ride it, and whoever needs its milk may drink it. And His saying, Then mention the name of God over them, standing in line. God Almighty says: So mention the name of God over the sacrificial animals when you slaughter them, standing in line. The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of reciters in the countries read it as mention the name of God over them, while they are in rows. The singular form is safa, and they were lined up in front of them. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Zaid bin Aslam, and another group with them, that they read it as sawafi with the ya in the accusative case, meaning: purely for God, with no partner for Him in it, pure for Him. Some of them read it as Sawaf, dropping the Ya and adding the Tanween to the letter, like Awar and Awwad. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he read it as Sawafin, meaning: Ma’qala. The correct reading of this, in my opinion, is the reading of those who read it with emphasis on the fa’ and its accusative, due to the consensus of the proof of the reciters on it with the meaning that we mentioned for those who read it in this way. Mention of those who interpreted it with the interpretation of those who read it with emphasis on the fa’ and its accusative: Abu Kuraib told us: Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Then mention the name of God over them while they stand in line, he said: God is greater, God is greater, O God, from You and for You. Standing in line: standing on three legs. So it was said to Ibn Abbas: What should we do with their hides? He said: Give them in charity and enjoy them. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: Ayoub bin Suwaid told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, standing, he said: standing. He said: He says: God is greater, there is no god but God, O God, from You and for You. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me: Ibn Abi Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then mention the name of God over them while standing in line. He said: Standing on three legs tied up, saying in the name of God, God is greater, God is from You and for You. Yaqoub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Hisin told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Standing in rows, he said: One of its hands is tied, he said: Standing on three legs. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, So mention the name of God over them while standing, he said: standing. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then mention the name of God over them, standing in line. And standing in line is that you tie one leg up, and line it up in three and slaughter it in that way. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Ya`la ibn Ata` told us, he said: Jubayr ibn Salim told me, he said: I saw Ibn Umar slaughtering his sacrificial animal, he said: So he said: Sawaf as God said, he said: So he slaughtered it while it was standing with one of its hands tied. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Laith told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Sawwaf: if she ties her leg and stands on three. He said: Laith told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then mention the name of God over them while they are in line. He said: Lined between their rows. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayj, on the authority of Mujahid, Sawaf he said: Standing on three legs. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Then mention the name of God over them while standing. He said: Between their duties while standing. Ibn al-Barqi told us: Ibn Maryam told us: Yahya ibn Ayoub told us, on the authority of Khalid ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah, that he used to slaughter sacrificial animals while they were standing facing the House, with their hands tied together. He said: They are the ones that God mentioned, So mention the name of God over them while they are in line. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told me, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I said to him about the statement of God, And mention the name of God over them while they are in line. He said: If you want to slaughter a sacrificial animal, slaughter it and say: God is Great, there is no god but God, O God, from You and for You, then say Bismillah, then slaughter it. I said: Should I say that for the sacrificial animal? He said: And for the sacrificial animal. Mention of those who interpreted it with the interpretation of those who read it as Sawafy with a Ya. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: So mention the name of God over them, sincerely. He said: Sincerely. He said: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Al-Hasan said: Sawafi: pure. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said: Al-Hasan said: Sawafi: purely for God. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Ayman ibn Nabil told us: I asked Tawus about his saying: And mention the name of God over them, clear. He said: Pure. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Yazid said, regarding His statement, So mention the name of God over them, while they are clear. He said: Pure, with no partner in them, as the polytheists used to do, making clear, pure, pure stones for God and their gods, for God Almighty. Mention of its interpretation according to the interpretation of those who read it as Sawafin. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, in the letter of Ibn Mas’ud: So mention the name of God over them, hanging upright. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada in the letter of Ibn Masoud: So mention the name of God over them, hanging upright. He said: That is, hanging upright. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Whoever reads it as Sawafin says: Reasonable. He said: Whoever reads it as Sawaf says: Describes the two hands of her. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Ma’ad say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Then mention the name of God over them, in rows, meaning in rows. And when a sacrificial animal is slaughtered, one hand is tied, so it is on three, and this is how it is slaughtered. Abu Jaafar said: The first of these statements was explained in the interpretation of his saying sawaf which is the one lined up in front of her, one of her legs tied. And his saying, And when its sides have set, he says: So when it falls and its sides fall to the ground after slaughtering, then eat from it, and it is from the saying of their strength: the sun has set: if it has set and fallen due to disappearance, and from it is the saying of Aws bin Hajar: Did not the sun, the moon and the planets eclipse the obligatory mountain? It means duty: reality. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told me, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So when its sides fall it falls to the ground. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, regarding his statement, Then when its sides are lowered, he said: When it is finished and slaughtered. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaid God bin Musa told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid: Then when it is due, it is slaughtered. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when its sides are lowered, he said: When it is slaughtered. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Then when her sides are cast down, he said: Then when she dies. His saying, Then eat from it, is interpreted as a command, and its meaning is: permission and generality. God says: So if you slaughter an animal and it falls dead after slaughtering, then it is permissible for you to eat it, and it is not an obligatory command. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i used to say about this: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: If he wants, he may eat, and if he wants, he may not eat. It is like And when you are in a state of ihram, then hunt (al-Ma’idah 5:2). Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So eat from it and feed the contented and the needy. He said: He eats from it and feeds. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Yunus informed us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, and Mughirah informed us, on the authority of Ibrahim, and Hajjaj informed us, on the authority of Ata’, and Hisin informed us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: Then eat from it, he said: If he wishes, he may eat, and if he wishes, he may not eat. Mujahid said: It is a concession, it is like His statement: So when the prayer is concluded, disperse throughout the land (al-Jumuah 62:10) and like His statement: And when you are in a state of ihram, then hunt (al-Ma’idah 5:2), and His statement: And feed the contented and the needy (al-Ma’idah 5:2) meaning: So feed from it the contented. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the contented and the one who objects. Some of them said: The contented is the one who is satisfied with what he has been given or with what he has and does not ask. And the one who objects is the one who objects to you feeding him meat and does not ask. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And feed the contented and the needy, he said: The contented is the one who is satisfied with what you have given him, and he is in his home. The one who objects: the one who approaches you and asks you to feed him meat without asking. These are the ones who were ordered to be fed meat. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The contented one is your neighbor who is satisfied with what you give him. And the one who begs is the one who approaches you and does not ask you. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Al-Qurazi, that he used to say regarding this verse: And feed the contented and the needy. The contented is the one who is content with a small thing and is satisfied with it. And the needy is the one who passes by you and does not ask for anything, so that is the needy. Others said: The contented one is the one who is satisfied with what he has and does not ask, and the one who asks you is the one who asks you. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: The contented and the needy means: the contented is the one who is self-restrained, and the needy means: the one who asks. Ibn Abi Al-Shawareb told us: Abd Al-Wahid told us: Khasif told us: I heard Mujahid say: Al-Qani’ is the people of Mecca, and Al-Mu’tar is the one who approaches you and asks you. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: He said: Ata’ told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Bashar told us: Muslim bin Ibrahim told us: Kaab bin Farukh told us: I heard Qatada narrating, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, the contented and the needy, he said: The contented is the one who sits in his house, and the needy is the one who asks. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The contented one is the one who is self-sufficient and sits in his house, and the one who asks you is the one who comes to you and asks you. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The contented and the one who asks, he said: The contented is the one who desires what is before you and does not ask you, and the one who asks is the one who approaches you and does not ask you. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman told me: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid and Ibrahim, who said: Al-Qani’ is the one sitting in his house, and Al-Mu’tar is the one who asks you. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada regarding the contented and the one who is content, he said: The contented is the one who is content in his hands, and the one who is content is the one who is at odds with you, and both of them have a right over you, O son of Adam. Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: So eat from it and feed the contented and the needy. He said: The contented is the one who sits in his house. And the needy is the one who begs you. Others said: The contented one is the one who is at ease, and the one who asks is the one who is begging you and does not ask. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Yunus told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said: The contented one is the one who is content with you and asks you, and the objector is the one who approaches you but does not ask you. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur Ibn Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding this verse: And feed the contented and the needy. He said: The contented is the one who is satisfied, and the needy is the one who begs you. He said: Al-Kalbi said: Al-Qani’ is the one who asks you, and Al-Mu’tadir is the one who confronts you, exposes himself but does not ask you. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And feed the contented and the needy, he said: The contented is the one who asks you, and the needy is the one who approaches you. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, he said: Saeed bin Jubair said: Al-Qani’ is the one who asks. Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told me, he said: Ghalib told me, he said: Sharik told me, on the authority of Furat Al-Qazzaz, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: the contented one, he said: He is the one who asks, then he said: Have you not heard the statement of Al-Shamakh: A person's wealth improves him and makes him rich. Poverty is more honorable than contentment. He said: From the question. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he said regarding His statement: And feed the contented and the needy, he said: The contented is the one who is content with you and asks you, and the needy is the one who shows himself to you and exposes himself to you and does not ask you. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Mansour and Yunus told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The one who is content is the one who asks, and the one who objects is the one who exposes himself and does not ask. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abdullah bin Ayyash told me, he said: Zaid bin Aslam said: The contented one is the one who asks people. Others said: Al-Qani’ is the neighbor, and Al-Mu’tar is the one who approaches you from among the people. Mention who said that. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Al-Qani’ is your neighbor, even if he is rich, and Al-Mu’tar is the one who begs you. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, who said: Mujahid said regarding his statement: And feed the contented and the needy, he said: The contented is your rich neighbor, and the needy is the one who has befallen you among the people. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: And feed the needy and the needy, he said: One of them is the beggar, and the other is the neighbor. Others said: Al-Qani’ is the one who walks around. Al-Mu’tar is the visiting friend. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: My father and Shuaib bin Al-Layth told me on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Khalid bin Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hilal, who said: Zaid bin Aslam said, regarding the words of God Almighty: The contented and the needy. The contented is the poor person who goes around, and the needy is the friend and the weak person who visits. Others said: Al-Qani’ is the greedy one, and Al-Mu’tarr is the one who groans with his body. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: the contented he said: the greedy and the needy: the one who needs his body, whether rich or poor. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Omar bin Ata’ told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: The contented one is the one who is greedy. Others said: Al-Qani’ is the poor person, and Al-Mu’tar is the one who is exposed to meat. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And feed the contented and the needy, he said: The contented is the poor, and the needy is the one who comes to the people for their meat and is not poor, and does not have a sacrifice, he comes to the people for their meat, and the wretched and needy is the contented. Others said: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Furat, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Al-Qani’ is the one who is content, and al-Mu’tar is the one who confronts you. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan, similarly. He said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim and Mujahid: The contented and the one who is asking for something. The contented is the one sitting in his house, and the one who is asking for something is the one who is asking for something from you. The first of these sayings to be correct is the saying of the one who said: “By ‘al-qani’ he meant the one who asks,’ because if what was meant by ‘al-qani’ in this context was the one who is content with what he has and is independent of it, it would have been said: ‘And feed the contented and the asker,’ and not said: ‘And feed the contented and the beggar.’ Following that is his saying: ‘And the beggar,’ the clear evidence that what is meant by ‘al-qani’ is the beggar,’ from their saying: ‘So-and-so was content with so-and-so,’ meaning he asked him and submitted to him, so he is content, contented. From this is the saying of Labid: And the Master gave me when I was poor, when he said, “See my solitude and my contentment!” As for the satisfied one, who means the satisfied one, it is from qana’at with a kasra on the letter noon, meaning he qana’an, qana’an, and qana’an. As for the one who asks, he is the one who comes to you asking for you to give him something and feed him. And His saying, Thus have We subjected them to you, means, Thus have We subjected the bodies to you, O people, “that you may be grateful,” meaning, that you may thank Me for subjecting them to you.
22:37: God Almighty says: Neither the flesh of your bodies nor their blood reaches God, but your piety towards Him reaches Him if you fear Him in it, intending thereby His face, and doing thereby what He has urged you to do and commanded you to do in its affair, and respecting thereby His sanctities. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding the statement of God: Neither their meat nor their blood reaches God, but what reaches Him is piety from you, he said: What is intended by it is the face of God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Neither their meat nor their blood reaches God, but what reaches Him is your piety, he said: If you fear God in this body, and work in it for God, and seek what God said to magnify the symbols of God and the sacred limits of God, for He said, And whoever honors the symbols of God, it is from the piety of the hearts (al-Hajj 22:30). He said: And whoever honors the sacred limits of God, it is better for him with his Lord (al-Hajj 22:32). He said: And He made it good, so that is what God accepts. As for the meat and blood, from where do they reach God? And His statement, Thus has He subjected them to you means: Thus has He subjected the bodies to you, that you may glorify God for having guided you means: so that you may glorify God for having guided you, meaning for His guiding you to His religion and to the rituals in your Hajj. As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: So that you may glorify God for guiding you. He said: For slaughtering it in those days. And give good tidings to the doers of good. He said: And give good tidings, O Muhammad, to those who obeyed God and did well in their obedience to Him in this world with Paradise in the Hereafter.
22:38: God the Almighty says: Indeed, God repels the evil of the polytheists from those who believed in God and His Messenger. Indeed, God does not love any traitor who betrays God, disobeys His commands and prohibitions, and obeys Satan. Ungrateful means: one who is ungrateful for His blessings upon Him, who does not recognize the right of the one who bestowed them, and does not thank Him for them. It was said that what he meant by this is: God repelled the polytheists of Quraysh from those who were among them of the believers before their migration.
22:39: God Almighty says: God has given permission to the believers who fight the polytheists in His cause because the polytheists have wronged them by fighting them. The reciters differed in reading this, so the majority of the reciters of Medina read it as adhan with a damma on the alif, and yuqātilūn with a fathah on the ta’, leaving out naming the agent, in udhan and yuqātilūn together. Some of the Kufians and the majority of the Basran reciters read it as udhan without naming the agent, and yuqātilūn with a kasrah on the ta’, meaning those who are permitted to fight fight the polytheists. The majority of the Kufian reciters and some of the Meccans read it as udhan with a fathah on the alif, meaning: God has permitted, and yuqātilūn with a kasrah on the ta’, meaning: those who God has permitted to fight fight the polytheists. These three readings are close in meaning, because those who read udhan in a way that does not name the agent, its meaning in interpretation goes back to the meaning of the reading of the reciters in a way that does name the agent. And whoever reads yuqātilūn and yuqātilūn with a kasrah or a fathah, the meaning of one of them is close to the meaning of the other. That is because whoever fights a human being, the one who fought him has a fighter, and each one of them is a fighter. If that is the case, then whichever of these readings the reader recites, he is correct. However, what I prefer is to read it with a fat-ha on the alif, meaning: God has given permission, because of its proximity to His statement, Indeed, God does not love any traitorous ingrate. God has given permission to those whom He does not love for those who fight them by fighting them, so permission is a response to His statement, Indeed, God does not love. Likewise, what I prefer to read in they fight is with a kasra on the ta’, meaning: those who fight those whom God has informed us about whom He does not love, so the speech is connected in meaning to one another. There is a difference of opinion about those who were meant by the permission given to them in this verse to fight. Some of them said: It meant: the Prophet of God and his companions. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: “Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought against because they have been wronged. And indeed, God is competent to give them victory,” meaning Muhammad and his companions when they were expelled from Mecca to Medina. God says, And indeed, God is competent to give them victory, and He did. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, left Mecca, a man said: They expelled their Prophet, so the following verse was revealed: Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought against because they were wronged… the verse those who were expelled from their homes without right the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. Yahya bin Dawud al-Wasiti narrated: Ishaq bin Yusuf narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, left Mecca, Abu Bakr said: They have expelled their Prophet. To God we belong and to Him we shall return. He will perish. Ibn Abbas said: Then God revealed: “Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged. And indeed, God is competent to give them victory.” Abu Bakr said: Then I knew that there would be fighting, and it was the first verse to be revealed. Ibn Dawud said: Ibn Ishaq said: They used to recite permission and we used to recite permission. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out, then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Abu Bakr said: I know that there will be fighting, and his hadith ended at this point, and he did not add anything to it. Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me: Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us: Qais ibn al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left Mecca, Abu Bakr said: “To God we belong and to Him we shall return. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been expelled, and by God they will all perish.” So when the verse was revealed: Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought against, because they have been wronged… to His saying: those who have been expelled from their homes without right, Abu Bakr knew that there would be fighting. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged, he said: He gave them permission to fight them after He pardoned them for ten years, and he read: Those who were expelled from their homes without right, and he said: These are the believers. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Concerning His statement: Those who were expelled from their homes without right. Others said: Rather, this verse refers to specific people who left the land of war, intending to emigrate, but were prevented from doing so. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Permission is given to those who are being fought against because they were wronged, he said: Believers left Mecca to Medina as emigrants, and they were prevented, so God gave permission to the believers to fight the infidels, so they fought them. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought against because they were wronged, he said: Some of the believers left Mecca to Medina as emigrants. They were being protected, but the infidels caught up with them, so permission was given to the believers to fight the infidels, so they fought them. Ibn Jurayj said: He said: The first fighting that God gave permission to the believers. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Abu Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, in the letter of Ibn Mas’ud: Permission is given to those who fight in the way of God. Qatada said: It is the first verse revealed about fighting, so they were given permission to fight. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, in His saying, Permission is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged. He said: It is the first verse revealed about fighting, so He gave them permission to fight. Some of them claimed that God only said, Permission is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged because the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill the infidels if they harmed them and were harsh on them in Mecca before the migration by treachery and secretly. So God revealed about that, Indeed, God does not like any traitorous ungrateful person. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions migrated to Medina, He gave them permission to kill and fight them, so He said, Permission is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged. This is a statement that was reported from Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim from an unproven source. And His saying: And indeed, God is able to give them victory. God Almighty says: And indeed, God is able to give victory to the believers who fight in the way of God. And He has given them victory, honored them, raised them up, and destroyed their enemy and humiliated them at their hands.
22:40: God the Most High says: Permission is given to those who are being fought against. Those who were expelled from their homes without right. The second those is a response to the first those who were expelled from their homes. What He meant by those who were expelled from their homes are the believers whom the infidels of Quraysh expelled from Mecca. They expelled them from their homes and tortured some of them for believing in God and His Messenger, and some of them insulted them with their tongues and threatened them, until they forced them to leave them. What they did to them was without right, because they were on falsehood, while the believers were on the truth. Therefore, He the Most High said: Those who were expelled from their homes without right. And His statement: Except that they say, ‘Our Lord is God.’ God the Most High says: They were not expelled from their homes except by saying, Our Lord is God alone, with no partner for Him. So an is in the accusative case in response to the ba in His statement: without right. It may be permissible for it to be in the accusative case as an exception. His saying: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: And had God not repelled the polytheists by means of the Muslims. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement: And had God not repelled some people by means of others means repelling the polytheists by means of the Muslims. Others said: The meaning of this is: Had it not been for fighting and jihad in the way of God. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, he said: Had it not been for fighting and jihad. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Had God not repelled the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from those who came after them from the followers. Who said that? Ibrahim bin Saeed told us: Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Saif bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Thabit bin Awsaja Al-Hadrami, who said: Twenty-seven of the companions of Ali and Abdullah told me, including Lahiq bin Al-Aqmar, Al-Aizar bin Jarwal, and Atiyah Al-Qurazi, that Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: This verse was revealed about the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, and had God not defended the followers through the companions of Muhammad, monasteries and churches would have been pulled down. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: If God had not repelled those whose testimony is required to be accepted in rights, it would be for some people over others, for those whose testimony is not permissible to accept, and others, so He revived that which is this, and because of that the shedding of this person’s blood would be prevented, and they left the injustices for his sake, for the injustice of the people, so the monasteries were demolished. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, he said: Some of them repel others in testimony, in the truth, and in what comes before this, he said: Had it not been for them, these monasteries and what was mentioned with them would have been destroyed. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty, mentioned that if it were not for the people defending each other, He would have destroyed what was mentioned, from His Almighty repelling some of them by others, and preventing the polytheists from doing that with the Muslims, and from that He prevented some of them from oppressing each other, like the ruler who prevents his subjects from oppressing each other, and from that He prevents the one who allows his testimony between them from taking the right of someone who has a right over him, and the like, and all of that is from Him repelling some of the people from each other, were it not for that they would have oppressed each other, so the conquerors destroyed the monasteries of the conquered and their churches, and what He, may His praise be glorified, named, and God Almighty did not put evidence in the mind that He meant some of that without others, nor did He bring that it is like that, a report that must be accepted, so therefore it is on the apparent and general as I have explained before, for the generality of the apparent meaning of that is all that we have mentioned. His saying: I would have demolished monasteries. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of monasteries. Some of them said: He meant the monasteries of monks. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abdul Wahhab told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Rafi’, regarding this verse: I would have demolished monasteries. He said: The monasteries of the monks. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: The monasteries would have been demolished, he said: The monasteries of the monks. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: I would have demolished monasteries. He said: The monasteries of the monks. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement: I would have demolished monasteries, he said: The monasteries of the monks. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Regarding His statement: I would have demolished monasteries, they are the monasteries of the little ones that they build. Others said: Rather, they are the monasteries of the Sabians. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul Ala told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Monasteries he said: They are for the Sabians. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement: to destroy. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as to destroy with a light lhadamat. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as to destroy with a shaddah, meaning to repeat the destruction in it time after time. The shaddah in that is more pleasing to me than the two readings, because that is what the disbelievers do with that. As for his saying: and sale, he means by it: the sale of Christians. The interpreters differed on this, and some of them said the same as we said on this. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdul-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Rafi’: And the sale, he said: The sale of the Christians. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And it was sold to the Christians. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: The sale: the sale of the Christians. Others said: What is meant by the sale in this place is the churches of the Jews. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: And a sale, he said: And churches. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement: And the sale, he said: The sale: the churches. His saying: And prayers. The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: What is meant by prayers are the churches. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And prayers, he said: He means by prayers the churches. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: and prayers: the churches of the Jews, and they call the church a prayer. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And prayers are the churches of the Jews. Others said: What he meant by prayers are the mosques of the Sabians. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us: I asked Abu Al-A’la about the prayers. He said: They are the mosques of the Sabians. He said: Abd al-Wahhab told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Rafi’, something similar. Others said: They are mosques for Muslims and the People of the Book on the roads. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement and prayers he said: Mosques for the People of the Book, and for the People of Islam on the roads. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement: And prayers, he said: The prayers are the prayers of the people of Islam, they are cut off if the enemy enters upon them, worship is cut off, and the mosques are demolished, as Nebuchadnezzar did. His saying: And mosques in which the name of God is much mentioned. There is a difference of opinion as to which mosques are meant by this statement. Some of them said: What is meant by this are the mosques of the Muslims. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Rafi’, his statement, and mosques, he said: the mosques of the Muslims. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: And mosques in which the name of God is much mentioned. He said: The mosques are the mosques of the Muslims in which the name of God is much mentioned. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. Others said: What he meant by his saying: and mosques are monasteries, churches, and prayer halls. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement: And mosques, he says that in all of this the name of God is mentioned frequently, and he did not specify the mosques. Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: Prayers are not destroyed, but he interpreted it as another action, as if he had said: And prayers were left. Some of them said: It means: the places of prayers. Some of them said: They are prayers, and they are the churches of the Jews, called in Hebrew: Salata. The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of this is: The monks’ monasteries, the Christians’ churches, and the Jews’ prayer rooms, which are their churches, and the Muslims’ mosques in which the name of God is often mentioned, would be demolished. We said that this statement is more deserving of interpretation, because that is what is known in the speech of the Arabs, and is widespread among them, and whatever statement contradicts it, even if it has a face, is not used in the way it is directed to. And His statement: And God will surely support those who support Him, the Most High says: And God will surely support those who fight in His cause, so that His word will be supreme over His enemy. So God’s support for His servant is His assistance to him, and the servant’s support for his Lord is his struggle in His cause, so that His word will be supreme. And His saying: Indeed, God is Strong and Mighty. God Almighty says: Indeed, God is Strong in giving victory to those who strive in His cause from among the people of His guardianship and obedience. He is Mighty in His kingdom. He says: He is impregnable in His authority. No conqueror can subdue Him, and no conqueror can overcome Him.
22:41: God the Most High says: Then for those who are fought because they have been wronged, who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, and those here are a response to those who are fought, and what He means by His saying: if We establish them in the land is that We give them a homeland in the country, so they conquer the polytheists, and overcome them over it, and they are the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, He says: If We grant them victory over their enemies, and they conquer the polytheists of Mecca, they obey God, so they establish prayer within its limits, and give zakat: He says: And give the zakat of their wealth to whom God has made it for. And enjoin what is right He says: And call people to the Oneness of God, and to work in obedience to Him, and what the people of faith in God know. And forbid what is wrong He says: And forbid associating partners with God, and working in disobeying Him, which the people of truth and faith in God reject. And to God belongs the outcome of matters He says: And to God belongs the end of creation, meaning: To Him is its destination in reward for it, and punishment in the Hereafter. The afterlife And in a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Husayn Al-Ashib told us, he said: Abu Ja`far `Isa bin Mahan, who is called Al-Razi, told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, regarding His statement: Those who, if We establish them in the land, will establish prayer and give zakah, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, he said: Their enjoining what is right was that they called to sincerity to God alone, with no partner for Him, and their forbidding what is wrong was that they forbade the worship of idols and the worship of Satan. He said: So whoever calls to God from among all people has enjoined what is right, and whoever forbids the worship of idols and the worship of Satan has forbade what is wrong.
22:42: God Almighty says, consoling His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the harm he suffers from the polytheists, and urging him to be patient with the insults and denials they inflict on him: And if these polytheists deny you, O Muhammad, for what you have brought them of truth and proof, and what you promise them of punishment for their disbelief in God, then that is the way of their brothers from the past nations who denied the messengers of God, who associated partners with God, and their way before them, so do not let that deter you, for the humiliating punishment is behind them and My victory for you and your followers over them, I will come to them from behind that, just as a punishment came to their ancestors from the nations who came before them, after the respite until the appointed times were reached, for before them, there were those who denied: meaning the polytheists of Quraysh, the people of Noah, the people of Aad, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the people of Lot, and the people of Madyan, who are the people of Shu`ayb: He says: All of these denied their messengers and Moses denied, so it was said: And he denied Moses, and he did not say: and the people of Moses, because the people of Moses are the Children of Israel, and they had responded to him and did not deny him, but rather Pharaoh from the Copts denied him. And it has been said: It was only said thus because he was born among them, as he was born among the people of Mecca. And His statement: So I granted respite to the disbelievers means: So I granted respite to the people of disbelief in God from these nations, so I did not hasten them with punishment and torment. Then I seized them means: Then I brought down the punishment upon them after the respite. How was My denunciation? means: So look, O Muhammad, how I changed the blessing that they had, and how I denied them the kindness I had shown them. Did I not replace their multitude with fewness, their life with death and destruction, and their prosperity with ruin? He says: So that is what I will do with those of Quraysh who denied you. If I grant them respite until their appointed times, then I will fulfill My promise to you regarding them, just as I fulfilled My promise to other messengers regarding their nations, so We destroyed them and saved them from among them.
22:43: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot.
22:44: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “And the companions of Madyan denied Moses, so I granted respite to the disbelievers, then I seized them. How terrible was My reproach.”
22:45: God the Almighty says: How many a town, O Muhammad, have You destroyed its people while they were wrongdoers. He says: They worshipped other than those who should be worshipped, and disobeyed those whom they should not disobey. And His statement: So they are desolate on their roofs means: Their people perished and they became empty, and they were devoid of their inhabitants, so they were ruined and collapsed, and their roofs collapsed, meaning on their buildings and roofs. Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said: Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: Its roofs are empty. He said: Its emptiness is its ruin, and its roofs are its ceilings. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Empty means: a ruin in which there is no one. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, similarly. And His statement: And a well that has been abandoned, God Almighty says: How many a town have We destroyed, and how many a well have We abandoned, by annihilating its people and killing those who came to it, so it was flooded and abandoned, with no one coming to it or drinking from it, and how many a lofty palace built of rocks and plaster, was emptied of its inhabitants, because We made its people taste Our punishment for their evil deeds, so they perished, and their lofty palaces remained empty of them. The well and the palace are in the genitive case in apposition to the town. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: They are conjoined with the thrones by conjoining them with it in the accusative case, even though it is not good in them, on the basis that the thrones are the highest of the houses, and the well is in the ground, and so is the palace, because the village did not appear after the palace, but rather he followed one another, as he said: And beautiful maidens with large eyes * Like pearls (al-Waqi’ah 56:22-23). So the meaning of the speech according to what he said is what we mentioned his statement in that, so how many a village did We destroy while it was unjust, so it is empty on its thrones, and it has a well that is not in use, and a lofty palace, but since there was no one with the well to raise it or work in it, he followed it in the syntax with the thrones, and the meaning is: what was described. And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying: And a well that is not in use, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And a neglected well. He said: The one that has been abandoned. And someone else said: It has no people. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And a well that was abandoned. He said: Its people abandoned it. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And a well that is unused, he said: It has no people. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his saying: And a lofty palace. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And a plastered palace. Who said that? Matar bin Muhammad Al-Dhabi told me, he said: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Khabab, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And a lofty palace, he said: plastered. Abu Kuraib told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hilal bin Khabab, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same. Al-Husayn bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told me: My father told me, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And a lofty palace, he said: plastered. Matar bin Muhammad told me: Kathir bin Hisham told us: Jaafar bin Burqan told us: I was walking with Ikrimah, and he saw a wall of molten bricks, so he put his hand on it and said: This is the building that God said. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Khabab, on the authority of Ikrimah, And a lofty palace. He said: plastered. Ikrimah said: Plaster in Medina is called shid. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And a palace built high, he said: with tiles or silver. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And a palace built, he said: with plaster, meaning with gypsum. Al-Qasim told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: And a lofty palace, he said: plastered. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Hilal ibn Khabab, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement: And a lofty palace, he said: Plastered. This is how it is in my book, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: a tall, thin palace. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And a lofty palace. He said: Its people had built it and fortified it, but they perished and abandoned it. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement: And a lofty palace, he said: Tall. The first of the two opinions on this matter is more correct: the opinion of the one who said: What is meant by ‘the built’ is the plastered one. This is because ‘the built’ in the speech of the Arabs is the plaster itself, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: Like a grain of water, the tayyib and the shiid Al-Mushaid: is the passive participle of the verb to build, and from this comes the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: In Tayma, there is not a single palm trunk or hill left without being built with a boulder. Meaning: Balka means: except for the construction with gypsum and boulders. It may be possible that what is meant by the constructed is: the one whose construction is raised with gypsum, so those who said: What is meant by the constructed is: the tall one, thus tended towards this interpretation, and from it is the saying of Adi bin Zaid: It is built of marble and covered with lime, so that the birds can nest in its peaks. Some scholars of Arabic language have interpreted it to mean decorated with plaster due to its intensity. Ashida: if you decorate it with it, and this is similar to the meaning of the one who said: plastered.
22:46: God Almighty says: Did not these deniers of the signs of God and those who denied His power travel through the lands and see the fates of their peers among the deniers of God’s messengers who passed away before them, such as ‘Aad and Thamud, and the people of Lot and Shu’aib, and their homelands and dwellings, so that they could reflect on them, take lessons from them, and learn from their contemplation of their affairs and the affairs of their people, God’s way with those who disbelieved and worshipped other than Him, and denied His messengers, so that they would turn from their insolence and disbelief, and if they contemplated that, took lessons from it, and turned to the truth, they would have hearts with which to understand God’s proofs to His creation and His power over what we have explained, or ears with which to hear: He says: Or ears that listen to the truth and comprehend it, and distinguish between it and falsehood. And His statement: For indeed, eyes are not blinded means: For indeed, their eyes are not blinded from seeing people and observing them, rather they see that with their eyes, but their hearts which are in their chests are blinded from seeing the truth and knowing it. The ha in His statement: For indeed, they are not blind is a ha of support, like the saying of the one who says: He is Abdullah standing. It has been mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah, for indeed, eyes are not blinded. And it has been said: But blind are the hearts which are in the chests, and hearts are only in the chests, to emphasize the statement, as it has been said: They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts Al-Imran 3:167.
22:47: God Almighty says: And the polytheists of your people are hastening you, O Muhammad, with what you promise them of God’s punishment for their polytheism with Him, and their denial of you in what you brought them from God in this world. And God will not fail in His promise that He promised you concerning them, of bringing His punishment and vengeance upon them in this world. So He did that, and fulfilled what He promised them, so He killed them on the Day of Badr. The people of interpretation differed regarding the day about which God Almighty said: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. He said: From the days in which God created the heavens and the earth. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And indeed, a Day with your Lord... the verse, he said: It is like his statement in Alif, Lam, Meem. It is an equal revelation, it is the same verse. Others said: Rather, it is one of the days of the Hereafter. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The length of the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection is a thousand years. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Saeed Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Sameer bin Nahar, he said: Abu Hurayrah said: The poor Muslims will enter Paradise before the rich by half a day. I said: What is half a day? He said: Do you not read the Qur’an? I said: Yes. He said: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Mujahid: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years. He said: Of the days of the Hereafter. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of `Ikrimah, that he said concerning this verse: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. He said: These are the days of the Hereafter. And concerning His statement: Then he will ascend to Him in a Day the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count. (Sajdah: 5), he said: The Day of Resurrection. And he recited: Indeed, they see it far off, but We see it near. (Al-Ma`arij: 6-7). There is a difference of opinion as to why the statement was changed from reporting the hastening of those who hastened the punishment to reporting the length of the day with God. Some of them said: The people hastened the punishment in this world, so God revealed: And God will not fail in His promise, that He would send down what He promised them of punishment in this world, and that a day with your Lord of their punishment in this world and the Hereafter is like a thousand years of what you count in this world. Others said: It was said thus as an announcement from God to those who hasten the punishment, that He does not hasten it, but rather He delays until the appointed time of His appointed time, and that what is slow in their view is near in His view. So He said to them: The measure of a day with Me is a thousand years of what you people count as your days, and it is slow in your view, but it is near in My view. Others said: The meaning of this is: A day of heaviness and what is feared is like a thousand years. The second statement is more likely to be true in my opinion, and that is that God, the Most High, mentioned that the polytheists hastened the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the punishment, then He mentioned the extent of the day with Him, then He followed that with His saying: And how many a town was I granted respite while it was unjust. So He mentioned that He granted respite to the people of the unjust town, and did not hasten to punish them, so He made clear with that that He meant by His saying: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count. So haste ceased from Himself, and He described it as patience and waiting. And since it is from your number, and that is not far from Him, and it is far from you, therefore He does not hasten to punish whomever He wants to punish, until he reaches the end of his term.
22:48: God the Almighty says: And how many a town have I granted respite to? He says: I granted them respite, and delayed their punishment, while they were polytheists with God, and disobeying His command, and that was their injustice with which God the Almighty described them, so I did not hasten their punishment. Then I seized it. He says: Then I seized it with punishment, so I punished it in this world by inflicting Our punishment upon them. And to Me is the destination. He says: And to Me is their destination also after their destruction, so they will receive from the punishment then what will not cease. God the Almighty says: So such is the case of those of your people who hastened your punishment, and if you grant them respite until their appointed terms that you have set for them, then I will seize them with punishment, so fight them with the sword, then to Me is their destination after that, so I will make them suffer as a punishment for the sins they have committed.
22:49: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people who argue with you about God without knowledge, following every rebellious devil: O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you. I warn you of God’s punishment that will descend upon you in My world, and His torment in the Hereafter that you will inflict. Clear: He says: I make my warning clear to you and show it, so that you may repent from your polytheism and beware of what I warn you of. I have no power over you other than that. As for hastening or delaying the punishment that you are hastening me to do, that is up to God. It is not up to me, and I cannot do it. Then he described his warning and his glad tidings, and did not mention the glad tidings. Since the warning was mentioned regarding an action, it was known that the glad tidings were the opposite, so he said: And those who believe in God and His Messenger and do righteous deeds among you, O people, and others, “for them is forgiveness meaning: for them from God is the covering of their past sins in this world for them in the Hereafter. And a generous provision meaning: and a good provision in Paradise. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, his statement, So those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and noble provision, he said: Paradise. And His statement, And those who strive against Our signs to frustrate them, means: And those who acted against Our proofs and turned people away from following Our Messenger and acknowledging Our Book that We revealed. And He said, Among Our signs, so in was included in it, just as it is said: So-and-so strived against the matter of so-and-so. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his saying, incapable. Some of them said: Its meaning is: making things difficult. Who said that? Ahmad bin Yusuf told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Ata’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he read it mu’ajizin in the entire Qur’an, meaning with an alif, and he said: mishaqin. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: In Our signs are those who are unable to do so. He said: They denied the signs of God, so they thought that they could do so without causing Him any difficulty, but they could never do so without causing Him any difficulty. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. These two aspects of interpretation are based on the reading of those who read it in Our verses there are miracles with an alif, and this is the reading of the general readers of Medina and Kufa. As for some of the readers of Mecca and Basra, they read it with a shaddah on the jim, without an alif, meaning that they rendered the people incapable and discouraged them from following the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believing in the Qur’an. It was mentioned by those who said that as well from his reading: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, slow down, he said: slow down, they slow down people from following the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. The correct thing to say about this is: They are two well-known readings, each of which was read by scholars of the reciters, and they are close in meaning. This is because whoever is unable to do the verses of God has been unable to do so. One of the ways to do so is to be unable to do so, and to act in disobedience to Him and disobey His command. The description of the people about whom God revealed these verses was that they were slow to prevent people from believing in God and following His Messenger, and they would struggle against the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), thinking that they would be able to defeat and overcome him, while God had guaranteed him victory over them.
