This was their way of doing so to God. If this is the case, then whichever of the two readings the reciter recites, he is correct in that. As for the miracle, it is the reciprocal of the word ajzah, and its meaning is: the struggle of two people, one of whom is his companion, whichever of them is unable to do so, the other overcomes and subdues him. As for the inability: it is the doubling and it is the activation from the inability. And his saying those are the companions of Hellfire he says: those who have this description are the inhabitants of Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection, and its people are its people.
22:50: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: So those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and noble provision.
22:51: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And those who strive against Our verses to frustrate them - those are the companions of Hellfire.
22:52: It was said that the reason for which this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was that Satan had put on his tongue, in some of what he recited, from what God had revealed to him of the Qur’an, what God had not revealed to him, so that was difficult for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was distressed by it, so God consoled him from what he was in with these verses. Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ma`shar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b Al-Qurazi and Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat in one of the clubs of the Quraysh, whose people were many, and he wished that day that nothing would come to him from God, so that they would flee from him. Then God revealed to him: ‘And by the star when it goes down, your companion has neither strayed nor has he erred’ (al-Najm 53:1-2). The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it until he reached: ‘Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-`Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other’ (al-Najm 53:19-20). Satan threw two words at him: ‘That is the highest scourge, and their intercession is indeed hoped for.’ So he spoke them, then he went on and recited the entire surah, and he prostrated at the end of the surah, and all the people prostrated with him. Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira raised some dirt to his forehead and prostrated on it, and he was a very old man who was not able to prostrate, so they were pleased with what he said and said: ‘We have understood.’” Indeed, God gives life and causes death, and it is He who creates and provides, but these gods of ours intercede for us with Him, since He has given them a share, so we are with you. They said: So when evening came, Gabriel, peace be upon them, came to him and recited the Surah to him. When he reached the two words that Satan had cast upon him, he said: I did not bring you these two. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have fabricated against God, and you have said about God what He did not say. So God revealed to him: And they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you, so that you might invent something else about Us. (al-Isra’ 17:73)... Until His saying: Then you will not find for yourself against Us a helper (al-Isra’ 17:75), so he remained sad and worried until the verse was revealed to him: “And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech. But God nullifies what Satan casts, and then God establishes His verses. And God is Knowing and Wise.” He said: So those who were from the emigrants in the land of Abyssinia heard that the people of Mecca had all converted to Islam, so they returned to their clans and said: They are dearer to us, and they found that the people had regressed when God nullified what Satan cast. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ziyad al-Madani, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw his people turning away from him, and he was distressed by what he saw of their distancing themselves from what he had brought to them from God, he wished in his heart that God would bring him something that would bring him closer to his people. And it pleased him, despite his love and concern for them, that He would soften some of what had been difficult for him regarding their affair, when he spoke to himself about that, and he wished and loved it, so God revealed: “And by the star when it goes down, your companion has not strayed, nor has he gone astray” (al-Najm 53:1-2). So when he reached the words of God: Have you considered al-Lat and al-‘Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other (al-Najm 53:19-20), Satan put on his tongue, when he was speaking to himself about it, and wishing that his people would bring it: Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is acceptable. So when the Quraysh heard that, they were happy and pleased, and they were amazed by what he had mentioned. And when he reached the prostration of it and concluded the surah, he prostrated in it, and the Muslims prostrated with the prostration of their Prophet, confirming what he brought, and following his command, and those in the mosque from the polytheists, from Quraysh and others, prostrated when they heard the mention of their gods, so there remained in the mosque no believer or disbeliever who did not prostrate, except for Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, for he was an old man and could not, so he took a handful of the plain with his hand, and prostrated on it, then the people dispersed from the mosque, and Quraysh came out and were pleased with what they heard of the mention of their gods, saying: Muhammad has mentioned our gods in the best way, and he claimed in what he recited that they are the high cranes, and that their intercession is accepted, and the prostration reached those in the land of Abyssinia from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said: Quraysh converted to Islam, Some of them stood up, while others stayed behind. Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, what have you done? You recited to the people what I did not bring to you from God, and you said what He did not say to you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saddened by that, and feared God greatly. Then God, the Blessed and Most High, sent down to him - and He was Merciful to him - to console him and make the matter easy for him, and to inform him that there was no Messenger or Prophet before him who wished as he wished, nor loved as he loved, except that Satan had cast into his wish what he cast on his tongue, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God abrogated what Satan cast, and perfected His verses, meaning that you are like some of the Prophets and Messengers. Then God sent down: And We did not send before you any Messenger or Prophet except that when he desired, Satan cast into his desire. The verse, so God removed the sadness from His Prophet, and secured him from what he feared, and abrogated what Satan put on his tongue of mentioning their gods, that they are the exalted cranes, and that their intercession is accepted, God says when He mentioned Al-Lat and Al-Uzza and Manat, the third other, until His saying: And how many are there angels in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except after God has given permission to whom He wills and is pleased with (al-Najm 53:26), meaning how can the intercession of your gods benefit Him? So when what came to him from God abrogated what Satan had put on the tongue of His Prophet, Quraysh said: Muhammad regretted what was the status of your gods with God, so other than that two letters that Satan put on the tongue of his Messenger have fallen into the mouth of every polytheist, so they increased in evil to what they were upon. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Al-Mu'tamir told us, he said: I heard Dawud from Abu al-'Aliyah, he said: The Quraysh said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Your companions are only the slave of Banu so-and-so and the client of Banu so-and-so. If you mentioned our gods with something, we would sit with you, for the nobles of the Arabs come to you, and when they see that your companions are the nobles of your people, they will desire you. He said: Then Satan put on his tongue: Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is hoped for, and the likes of them are not forgotten. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated when he read it, and the Muslims and polytheists prostrated with him. When he knew what had come to his tongue, it was difficult for him, so God revealed: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he desired, Satan cast into his desire... until His saying: And God is Knowing and Wise. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Al-Walid told us: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, who said: Quraysh said: O Muhammad, only the poor, the needy, and the weak of the people sit with you. If you mentioned our gods in a good way, we would sit with you, for people come to you from all over the world. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surat An-Najm. When he finished with this verse: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other? (al-Najm 53:19-20), Satan put on his tongue: And they are the great gharaniqa, and their intercession is hoped for. So when he finished, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated, along with the Muslims and the polytheists, except for Ahyiha Saeed bin Al-As. He took a handful of dirt and prostrated on it, and said: It is time for Ibn Abi Kabsha to mention our gods in a good way. Until the Muslims who were in Abyssinia from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were informed that Quraysh had become Muslim. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was greatly distressed by what Satan had put on his tongue. On his tongue, God revealed, And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet... to the end of the verse. Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, he said: When this verse was revealed: Have you considered al-Lat and al-`Uzza? (53:19), the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it and said: Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated himself, and the polytheists said: He did not mention your gods with any good before today. So the polytheists prostrated themselves with him, and God revealed: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech.... to His saying: The punishment of a barren Day. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-Samad told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, he said: Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, he said when the verse Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? (al-Najm 53:19) was revealed, then he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech, to His statement, And God is Knowing and Wise. That is because while the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying, the story of the gods of the Arabs was revealed to him, so he began to recite it and the polytheists heard him and said: We hear him mention our gods with goodness, so they approached him, and while he was reciting it and he was saying, Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other? (al-Najm 53:19-20), Satan cast: Indeed, those are the exalted cranes, from them intercession is hoped, so he began to recite it, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down and transformed it, then he said to him, And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech, to His statement, And God is Knowing and Wise. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn who said: I heard Abu Muadh saying: Ubayd told us, he said: I heard Ad-Dahhak saying regarding His statement, And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet… the verse, that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca, and God revealed to him about the gods of the Arabs, so he began to recite Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, and he repeated them frequently. The people of Mecca heard the Prophet of God mentioning their gods, so they rejoiced at that, and they came close to listen, so Satan threw into the recitation of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Those are the exalted cranes, from them intercession is hoped for, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it like that, so God revealed to him: And We did not send before you any messenger… to And God is Knowing and Wise. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, that he was asked about the statement of God, And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet... the verse. Ibn Shihab said: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Mecca, recited to them And the star when it goes down (al-Najm 53:1). When he reached Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other (al-Najm 53:19-20), he said: Their intercession is hoped for. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgot, and the polytheists in whose hearts was disease met him, and they greeted him, and were happy about that. He said to them: That is from Satan. Then God revealed And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet... until he reached Then God abrogates what Satan casts. The interpretation of the statement: O Muhammad, no messenger was sent before you to any nation, nor was there a prophet who spoke and was not sent, except if he wished. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his saying he wished in this place, and I mentioned the statement of a group of those who said that wish from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, what his soul told him of his love to approach his people, in mentioning their gods with some of what they love, and whoever said that out of love from him in some circumstances, not to mention with evil. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: if he reads, recites, or narrates. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying, When he wishes, Satan casts into his wish, meaning: When he speaks, Satan casts into his speech. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, If he wishes, he said: If he said. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, except when he wishes, meaning by wishing: recitation and reading. This statement is more like the interpretation of the quantity, as indicated by his saying, Then God abrogates what Satan casts, then God establishes His verses, on that, because the verses that God, may He be glorified and exalted, informed us that He establishes are undoubtedly verses of His revelation. So it is known that what Satan cast into it is what God, may He be glorified and exalted, informed us that He abrogated and nullified, then established it by abrogating that from it. The interpretation of the statement then is: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he recited the Book of God, and read, or spoke and narrated, Satan cast into the Book of God that he recited and read, or into his speech that he narrated and spoke, so God abrogates what Satan casts. God Almighty says: So God removes what Satan casts of that on the tongue of His Prophet and nullifies it. As Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then God abrogates what Satan casts, so God nullifies what Satan casts. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Then God abrogates what Satan casts, Gabriel abrogates by God’s command what He left on the tongue of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God perfected His verses. And His saying, Then God will establish His verses, means: Then God will purify the verses of His Book from the falsehood that Satan put on the tongue of His Prophet. And God is Knowing of what happens in His creation, nothing is hidden from Him. Wise in His management of them, and His diversion of them as He wills and loves.
22:53: God Almighty says: Then God abrogates what Satan casts, then God establishes His verses, so that He may make what Satan casts into the wish of His Prophet false, like the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is hoped for as a trial. He says a test that tests those in whose hearts is a disease of hypocrisy, and that is doubt in the truthfulness of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the truth of what he tells them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wished that God would not criticize the gods of the polytheists, but Satan cast doubt on his wish, saying: The gods whose intercession they claim are to be hoped for, and they are the exalted ones. So God abrogated that, and the rulings of God are His verses, Have you considered al-Lat and al-‘Uzza? until he reached whose authority? (al-Najm 53:23). Qatada said: When Satan cast what he cast, the polytheists said: God has spoken well of their gods, so they rejoiced at that, and then he mentioned His statement: That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is disease. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, That He may make what Satan throws in a trial for those in whose hearts is disease, he said: And for those whose hearts have hardened from believing in God, so they do not soften or show restraint, and they are the polytheists who associate others with God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, and those whose hearts are hardened, he said: the polytheists. And His statement, And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension, God Almighty says: Indeed, the polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, are in opposition to God’s command, far from the truth.
22:54: God Almighty says: And so that the people of knowledge of God may know that what God has sent down of His verses, which He has made perfect for His Messenger, and abrogated what Satan had cast into it, is the truth from your Lord, O Muhammad, so that they may believe in it: He says: So that they may believe in it, and their hearts may submit to it: He says: So that their hearts may submit to the Qur’an, and may acquiesce in believing in it, and acknowledging what is in it. And indeed, God is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path. And indeed, God is the Guide of those who believe in God and His Messenger to the intended truth, and the clear truth, by abrogating what Satan had cast into the wish of His Messenger, so that Satan’s plot and his casting of falsehood on the tongue of their Prophet may not harm them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord. He said: He means the Qur’an.
22:55: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieve in God will continue to be in doubt. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the letter ha’ in his statement: From him, from the mention of what it is. Some of them said: It is from the mention of the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is hoped for. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it, from His statement: Those are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is hoped for. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it, he said: What Satan brought will not leave their hearts, and it will increase their misguidance. Others said: Rather, it is from the mention of the prostration of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in An-Najm. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad told us: Shu’bah told us: Abu Bishr told us on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it. He said: In doubt about your prostration. Others said: Rather, it is from the mention of the Qur’an. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it. He said: Of the Qur’an. The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: It is a metaphor for mentioning the Qur’an whose verses God has perfected. This is because this is closer to mentioning His statement, And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, than mentioning His statement, So God abrogates what Satan casts, and the ha of His statement that it is from mentioning the Qur’an. So attaching the ha in His statement, in doubt thereof, to the ha of His statement, that it is the truth from your Lord is more appropriate than attaching it to what is in His statement, what Satan casts, despite the distance between them. And His statement, until the Hour comes to them, means: These disbelievers will remain in doubt about the matter of this Qur’an until the Hour comes to them suddenly, which is the hour when people will be gathered for the place of reckoning, suddenly. He says: suddenly, or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day. The people of interpretation differed about this day. Which day is it? Some of them said: It is the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: An old man from Khorasan from Azd, whose nickname was Abu Sasan, told us, he said: I asked Ad-Dahhak about his saying, The punishment of a barren day. He said: The punishment of a day after which there is no night. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, that the Day of Resurrection has no night. Others said: Rather, it refers to the day of Badr. And Wa said: It was only called the day of Aqeem, because they did not look at the night, so it was barren for them. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The torment of a barren day is the day of Badr. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day. Ibn Jurayj said: A day in which there is no night, they did not debate until night. Mujahid said: The punishment of a great day. He said: K narrated to us Al-Hussein said: Abu Tamila narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, he said: Mujahid said: The day of Badr. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Abu Idris told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, The punishment of a barren day, he said: The day of Badr. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, The punishment of a barren day, he said: It is the day of Badr, he mentioned it on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, The punishment of a barren day, he said: It is the day of Badr, on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b. This second statement is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse, because there is no reason to say: They will remain in doubt about it until the Hour comes to them suddenly, or the Hour comes to them, and that is because the Hour is the Day of Resurrection, since the barren day is also the Day of Resurrection, so its meaning is what we said about repeating the mention of the Hour twice, with different words, and that is meaningless. So since that is the case, then the most appropriate of the two interpretations is the one that is more correct in meaning, and more similar to what is known in the discourse, and that is what we mentioned in its meaning. The interpretation of the statement then is: And those who disbelieved will remain in doubt about it, until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, and they are sent to the eternal punishment, or the punishment of a day that will be barren for them comes to them, and they will not look forward to the night, nor will they be delayed until the evening, but they will be killed before the evening.
22:56: God Almighty says: The authority and the kingdom when the Hour comes will belong to God alone, with no partner for Him, and no one will dispute with Him on that Day. There were kings in the world who were called by this name, and no one on that Day will be called a king other than Him. He judges between them means: He separates between those who associate others with Him and those who believe. So those who believed in this Qur’an, and in the One who revealed it, and the One who brought it, and acted according to what is in it of what is permissible and what is forbidden, and its limits and its obligations, will be in the Gardens of Bliss on that Day. And those who disbelieved in God and His Messenger, and denied the verses of His Book and its revelation, and said: This is not from God, it is only a lie that Muhammad invented, and other people helped him in it, For those is a humiliating punishment. He says: So those who are like this will have a humiliating punishment with God on the Day of Resurrection, meaning a humiliating punishment in Hell.
22:57: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - for them is a humiliating punishment.
22:58: God the Almighty says: And those who left their homelands and their tribes, and left that for the sake of God's pleasure and obedience and jihad against His enemies, and then were killed or died while they were in that state, God will surely provide for them on the Day of Resurrection in His Gardens with a good provision. By good, He means generous, and what is meant by good provision is the abundant reward. And indeed, God is the Best of Providers. He says: And indeed, God is the Best of those who extend His grace to the people of His obedience and honor them. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who differed regarding the ruling on one who died in the cause of God. Some of them said: The one who was killed among them is the same as the one who died, and others said: The one who was killed is better. So God revealed this verse to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to teach them that the matter of the one who died in His cause and the one who was killed in it is the same in terms of reward with Him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shuraih told me, on the authority of Salaman ibn Amir, he said: Fadala was the emir of the quarters, and he went out with the funeral processions of two men, one of whom was killed and the other deceased, and he saw the people leaning towards the grave of the deceased man, so he said: I see you, O people, leaning towards the deceased man, and preferring him over his deceased brother, so by the One in Whose hand is my soul, I do not care which of their two graves I am sent from. Read the words of God Almighty: And those who emigrated for the cause of God and were killed or died... to His saying: And indeed, God is Knowing and Forbearing.
22:59: God Almighty says: God will surely admit those who are killed in His cause from among the emigrants and those who die from them to an entrance with which they will be pleased, and that entrance is Paradise. And God is Knowing of those who emigrate in His cause from those who leave their homes seeking booty, or worldly goods, Forbearing of the disobedient among His creation, by not treating them with punishment and torment.
22:60: God Almighty means by His saying that for those who migrated for the sake of God, then were killed or died, and for them also that God promises them victory over the polytheists who transgressed against them and expelled them from their homes. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: “That is so. And whoever punishes with the like of that with which he was punished.” He said: They are the polytheists who rebelled against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God promised him that He would support him. He also said about retaliation. Some of them claimed that this verse was revealed about a group of polytheists who encountered a group of Muslims on the last two nights of Muharram. The Muslims hated fighting during those days in the sacred months, so the Muslims asked the polytheists to stop fighting them for the sake of the sanctity of the month, but the polytheists refused and fought them, so they transgressed against them. The Muslims stood firm against them and were victorious over them. Then God revealed this verse: “That is so. And whoever retaliates with the like of that with which he was afflicted and then is transgressed against,” by initiating the fighting while he is averse to it, God will surely aid him. And His statement: Indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving, God Almighty says: Indeed, God is the possessor of pardon and forgiveness for whoever retaliates against someone who wronged him after the wrongdoer has wronged him with right. Forgiving of what he did to the one who initiated the injustice, like what he did to him, without punishing him for it.
22:61: He, the Most High, means by His saying: That is this victory that I grant him over the one who transgressed against him, over the transgressor, because I am able to do whatever I will. So from His power is that God merges the night into the day, meaning: He merges whatever hours of the night are missing into the hours of the day, so whatever is missing from this, He increases in this. And He merges the day into the night and He merges whatever hours of the day are missing into the hours of the night, so whatever is missing from the length of this, He increases in the length of this. And by the power that does that, He grants victory to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions over those who transgressed against them and expelled them from their homes and their wealth. And that God is Hearing and Seeing meaning: And He also did that by being the One who hears what they say of speech, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He is Seeing of what they do, nothing of it is hidden from Him, all of that is visible and heard from Him, and He is the Preserver of all of that, until He rewards all of them for what they said and did of speech and action with His reward.
22:62: God the Most High means by His saying that this action that I did of making the night enter the day, and making the day enter the night, because I am the Truth who has no equal, no partner, and no peer, and that which these polytheists call a god besides Him is falsehood that is not able to create anything, rather He is the created, God the Most High says to them: Will you abandon, you ignorant ones, the worship of the One from Whom is benefit and in Whose hand is harm, and He is able to do all things, and everything is below Him, and you worship falsehood whose worship does not benefit you? And His saying and that God is the Most High, the Great means by His saying: The Most High the One who is high above everything, He is above everything below Him, the Great means the Great, to whom everything is below Him, and nothing is greater than Him. Ibn Jurayj used to say about his statement, And that which they invoke besides Him is falsehood, what: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding His statement, And that which they invoke besides Him is falsehood, he said: Satan. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, And that which they call upon besides Him. The majority of the reciters of Iraq and the Hijaz read it as ta’ as a direct address, and the majority of the reciters of Iraq other than Asim read it as ya’ as a statement, and the ya’ is the more pleasing of the two readings to me, because the beginning of the statement is in the form of a direct address.
22:63: God Almighty says, Have you not seen, O Muhammad, that God sends down water from the sky meaning rain and the earth becomes green with what grows in it of plants God is Subtle in extracting plants from the earth with that water and other than that, from the innovation of what He wills to invent Aware of what happens from that plant of grain and with it. And He said and the earth becomes so He raised it, and His saying Have you not seen would have been absent from it, and it was said thus, because the meaning of the speech is report, as if it was said: Know, O Muhammad, that God sends down water from the sky and the earth becomes, and similar to that is the saying of the poet: Didn't you ask the old quarter and it spoke? And will the desert of Samlaq tell you today? Because it means: I asked him and he spoke.
22:64: God Almighty says: He owns whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. They are His servants, His slaves, and His creation. He has no partner in that, nor in anything of it. Indeed, God is independent of everything in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of His creation, and they are the ones in need of Him. He is the Praiseworthy before His servants for His favors upon them and His favors toward them.
22:65: God Almighty says: Have you not seen that God has subjected to you, O people, whatever is on the earth of animals and beasts? All of that is yours, and you can use it as you wish of your needs. And the ships sail through the sea by His command. He says: And He has subjected to you the ships sailing through the sea by His command, meaning by His power, and His making them subservient to you is like that. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement: And the ships sail. The majority of reciters in the countries read it as and the ships in the accusative case, meaning He has subjected to you whatever is on the earth, and the ships in apposition to what, and on the repetition of that and that the ships sail. It was narrated on the authority of Al-A’raj that he read it in the nominative case as the beginning, and the accusative case is the reading according to us in that, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it. And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth, meaning: And He holds back the sky by His power, so that it does not fall upon the earth except by His permission. The meaning of his saying: that it should not fall is that it should not fall. Indeed, God is to the people Most Kind and Merciful meaning: He is compassionate and merciful to them. Out of His compassion and mercy for them, He held back the sky from falling to the earth except by His permission, and He subjected to you what is described in this verse as a favor from Him to you.
22:66: God Almighty says: And God, who has bestowed these blessings upon you, is the one who made for you living bodies with a life that We created in you, and you were nothing. Then He will cause you to die after your life, and He will destroy you when your appointed times come, then He will bring you to life after your death when you are resurrected for the Hour of Resurrection. Indeed, man is ungrateful. He says: Indeed, the son of Adam is ungrateful for the blessings of God that He bestowed upon him from His good creation of him, and His subjecting to him what He subjected to what is on the earth by his worshipping other than Him of gods and rivals, and his abandoning the worship of Him alone, and the devotion of monotheism to Him alone. And His statement: For every nation We have appointed rites. He says: For every group of people who passed away before you, We have appointed a place to which they are accustomed, and a place to which they are accustomed, for My worship in it, and to perform My obligations, and a deed they are obligated to do. The root of the rite in the speech of the Arabs is the usual place that a man is accustomed to and becomes accustomed to, for good or evil. The rites of Hajj were named thus because people frequent the places where the rites of Hajj and Umrah are performed. There are two dialects for it: Mansik with a kasra on the seen and a fatha on the meem, and that is from the language of the people of Hijaz, and Mansik with a fatha on the meem and the seen together, and that is from the language of Asad, and it has been read in both languages. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His statement: For every nation We have appointed rites. Which rites did He mean by it? Some of them said: He meant by it: their festival that they are accustomed to. Who said that? Ali Naqal told me: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: For every nation We have appointed a ritual which they must observe, meaning: a festival. Others said: What he meant by it is: a slaughter that they slaughter, and blood that they shed. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told me, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: For every nation We have appointed rites which they must perform, he said: The shedding of blood in Mecca. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Rawqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: They are its devotees, he said: Shedding the blood of the sacrificial animals. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: A ritual he said: slaughtering and performing Hajj. The correct thing to say about this is: He meant by that the shedding of blood on the days of sacrifice at Mina, because the rituals about which the polytheists argued with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) were the shedding of blood on these days. They had argued with him about shedding the blood of the slaughtered animals, as God had informed us about in Surat Al-An`am, but those were not rituals. As for those that are rituals, they are gifts or sacrifices. Therefore we said: What is meant by the ritual in this place is the slaughter that is in the manner we have described. And His statement: So let them not dispute with you in the matter, the Most High says: So let these polytheists not dispute with you, O Muhammad, in your slaughter and your rituals by saying: Do you eat what you have killed, but do not eat the dead animal that God has killed? For you are more deserving of the truth than they are, because you are in the right and they are in the wrong. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Mention of those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: So let them not dispute with you in the matter. He said: Slaughtering. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So let him not dispute with you in the matter means do not be stubborn. And His saying: And call to your Lord means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And call, O Muhammad, those who dispute with you from the polytheists regarding your rituals and your slaughtering, to follow the command of your Lord in that, that they do not eat except what they slaughtered after following you, and after believing in what you have brought from God, and avoid slaughtering to gods and idols, and disavow them, for you are on a straight path, not deviating from the path of truth and correctness in your rituals that your Lord has made for you and your nation, and they are the ones who have gone astray in their intention of the path, for their disobedience to the command of God in their slaughterings and their food and their worship of gods.
22:67: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “For every nation We have appointed rites which they must perform. So let them not dispute with you in the matter and invite to your Lord. Indeed, you are on a straight path.”
22:68: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If these polytheists argue with you, O Muhammad, about your rituals, then say: God knows best what you do and what we do. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And if they argue with you, he said: The statement of the polytheists: As for what God has slaughtered with His right hand, “say: God knows best what you do,” for us our deeds and for you your deeds. And His statement: God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ. God Almighty says: And God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ in your religious affairs. Then you will know, O polytheists, who is right and who is wrong.
22:69: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ.
22:70: God Almighty says: Did you not know, O Muhammad, that God knows everything in the seven heavens and the seven earths? Nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He is the Judge between His creation on the Day of Resurrection, with knowledge of everything they did in this world. So He will reward the good among them for their good, and the evildoer for their evil. Indeed, that is in a Book: God Almighty says: His knowledge of that is in a Book, and it is the Mother of the Book in which our Lord, may His praise be glorified, wrote before He created His creation, and what will be until the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, that is easy for God. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Maysar bin Ismail Al-Halabi told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Abdah bin Abi Lubabah, he said: God knew what He would create and what the creation would do, then He wrote it down and then He said to His Prophet, “Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a record. Indeed, that, for God, is easy.” Al-Qasim told us: Al-Husayn told us: Maysar told us, on the authority of Arta’ah ibn al-Mundhir, who said: I heard Damrah ibn Habib say: God was on His throne over the water, and He created the heavens and the earth in truth, and He created the pen, and with it He wrote what would come of His creation, then that book glorified God and labored for a thousand years, before He began any of the creation. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he asked Ka’b al-Ahbar about the Mother of the Book, and he said: God knows what He is creating and what He created is working, so He said about His knowledge, Be a book. Ibn Jurayj used to say, in his statement: That is in a book: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, That is in a book. He said: His statement: God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ. We chose the statement we made about that, because his saying: That to his saying: Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth is closer than his saying: God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ, so attaching that to what is closer to it was more appropriate than what comes after it. His saying: Indeed, that is easy for God is disputed. Some of them said: Its meaning is that the judgment between those who differ in this world on the Day of Resurrection is easy for God. Mention of those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Indeed, that is easy for God. He said: His judgment on the Day of Resurrection. Then he said between that: Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a book. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that the Book of the Pen which God commanded to write on the Preserved Tablet whatever is to happen is easy, meaning simple. This second statement is more appropriate for the interpretation of this. This is because His statement: Indeed, that is easy for God… to His statement: Indeed, that is in a Book is closer and is adjacent to it, and from His statement: God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection it is far removed with the inclusion of His statement: Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth between them, so attaching it to what is closer is more appropriate for the speech and it is also a correct interpretation.
22:71: God Almighty says: And these polytheists worship besides God, what He, the Most High, has not sent down to them as proof from heaven in any of His books that He sent down to His messengers, that they are gods that are fit to be worshipped, so they worship them, because God has given them permission to worship them, and what they have no knowledge of that they are gods. And there is no helper for the wrongdoers. He says: And there is no helper for the disbelievers in God who worship these idols to aid them on the Day of Resurrection, to save them from God’s punishment, and to ward off His punishment from them if He wants to punish them.
22:72: God Almighty says: “And when Our verses are recited to the polytheists of Quraysh who worship besides God that for which He had not sent down any authority, ‘clear’ meaning: the verses of the Qur’an, ‘clear’ meaning: clear arguments and evidence for what they were revealed about, ‘you will recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve the evil’ meaning: you will recognize in their faces what the people of faith in God reject of their change, because of their hearing of the Qur’an. His statement: “They almost assault those who recite to them Our verses” means: They almost assault those who recite to them the verses of the Book of God from among the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of their intense hatred of hearing the Qur’an recited to them. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of his saying: they rob, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: They almost assault means: they strike. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: They almost attack means: They attack those whom he mentioned. Muhammad bin Amara told us: Abdullah bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid: They almost attack those who recite to them Our verses. He said: They almost fall upon them. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: They almost assault he said: They assault the infidels of Quraysh. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: They almost seize those who recite to them Our verses, meaning: They almost seize them by the hand. And His statement: “Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that?” He says: Shall I inform you, O polytheists, of something more hateful to you than those whose recitation you hate? It is the Fire that God promised to those who disbelieved. It was mentioned from some of them that he used to say: The polytheists said: By God, Muhammad and his companions are the worst of God’s creation. So God said to them: Say: Shall I inform you, O you who say this statement, of something worse than Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him? You, O polytheists, are the ones whom God has promised the Fire. And the Fire was raised as a subject, and because it is definite it is not suitable to describe evil with it, and it is indefinite, as it is said: I passed by two men: your brother and your father. If it were in the genitive case it would be permissible, and likewise if it were in the accusative case for the pronoun from mentioning it in its promise, and you intended by it to connect with what came before it. God the Almighty says: So these are the worst of creation, not Muhammad and his companions. And his saying: And what an evil destination means: And what an evil place these polytheists will end up in on the Day of Resurrection.
22:73: God Almighty says: O people, He has made a likeness and a remembrance for God. The meaning of striking in this place is: He made from their saying that He struck the authority over the people with the mission, meaning: He made it upon them, and He struck the jizya on the Christians, meaning: He made that upon them. The likeness is the resemblance. God Almighty says: He made a likeness for me, O people. He means by the likeness and the resemblance: the gods. He says: The polytheists and idols made a likeness for me, so they worshipped them with me, and associated them in my worship. So listen to Him. He says: So listen to the state of what they likened and made a likeness for me in their worship of Him. And its description is: Indeed, those you call upon besides God will never create a fly. He says: All that you worship besides God of the gods and idols, if they were gathered together, they would not create a fly in its smallness and kill it, because they are not able to do that and cannot bear it, and if they were all gathered together, they would create it. The fly is singular, and its plural in rare cases is adhbah, and in many cases it is dhabban, similar to gharab, and in rare cases it is aghrabah, and in many cases it is ghuraban. And his saying: And if the fly should steal something from them, meaning: And if the gods and idols should steal something from the flies of perfume or something similar to it, they would not be able to rescue it from him. He says: The gods are not able to rescue that from him. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of his saying: The seeker and the sought are weak. Some of them said: By the seeker he meant the gods, and by the sought he meant the flies. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said, in his statement: The seeker has become weak, he said: their gods, and the sought: the fly. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: The weakness of the one who asks from the sons of Adam to the idol is his need and what is requested from the idol is that he gives the one who asks from the sons of Adam what he asked for. He says: He is weak and unable to do that. The correct statement regarding this, according to us, is what I mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that its meaning is: The seeker, who is the gods, was unable to rescue from the fly what it had stolen from them, which is perfume and the like, and the sought-after is the fly. Rather, I said that this statement is more deserving of interpretation, because it is in the context of the report about the gods and the flies, so that it is more likely to be a report about what is connected to it than a report about what is disconnected from it. Rather, the Most High, His praise, informed about the gods with what He informed about them in this verse of their weakness and humiliation, as a rebuke from Him for that to their worshippers from the polytheists of Quraysh. The Most High, His mention, says: How can He make an example in worship, and associate in it with Me that which has no power to create a fly, and if He took the fly and took something from it, it would not be able to resist it, nor would it be victorious, and I am the Creator of what is in the heavens and the earth, and the Owner of all that, and the Giver of life to whomever I will and whomever I will? The one who does that is undoubtedly in the utmost ignorance. And his saying: They did not appreciate God with His true appreciation means: These people who made gods partners with God in worship did not appreciate His true appreciation when they associated others with Him, so they did not sincerely worship Him nor did they know Him with the true appreciation of their saying: I did not recognize so-and-so’s worth when they addressed with that someone who fell short in his right, and they wanted to glorify him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And if a fly should steal something from them... to the end of the verse, he said: This is an example of God’s blow to their gods, and he recited: “Weak are the seeker and the sought. They do not esteem God with His true esteem” when they worship with God something that cannot be vindicated by a fly and cannot protect itself from it. And His statement: Indeed, God is Strong means: Indeed, God is Strong in creating whatever He wills, from the small of His creation and the great of it. Mighty: He says: He is impregnable in His kingdom, and nothing besides Him is able to take away anything from His kingdom, and He is not like your gods, O polytheists, whom you call upon besides Him, who are not able to create a fly, nor to resist the fly, if it takes away something from it, weakness and humiliation.
22:74: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “They do not estimate God with His true estimate. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might.”
22:75: God Almighty says: God chooses messengers from among the angels, such as Gabriel and Michael, whom He used to send to His prophets, and whomever He wills from among His servants and from among the people, like His prophets whom He sent to His servants from among the children of Adam. The meaning of the words is: God chooses messengers from among the angels, and messengers from among the people as well. It has been said: This verse was revealed when the polytheists said: The Reminder was sent down to him from among us, so God said to them: That is up to Me and in My hand, not My creation. I choose whomever I will from among them for the message. And his saying: Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing means: Indeed, God is All-Hearing, what the polytheists said about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought from his Lord, and All-Seeing of whomever He chooses for His message from among His creation.
22:76: God Almighty says: God knows what was in the hands of His angels and messengers, before He created them and what is behind them. He says: And He knows what will happen after their demise. And to God all matters will return. He says: To God in the Hereafter the matters of this world will return, and to Him they will return as they were from Him in the beginning.
22:77: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, bow down to God in your prayers, prostrate to Him therein, worship your Lord, meaning: and humble yourselves before your Lord, and submit to Him in obedience, “and do good,” which your Lord has commanded you to do, that you may succeed, meaning: that you may succeed by doing so, and thereby attain your requests from your Lord. The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “And strive for God with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty - the religion of your father Abraham. He named you Muslims before and in this [religion] that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people.” The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying: And strive in the cause of God with the striving due to Him. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And strive against the polytheists in the cause of God with the striving due to Him. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Sulayman ibn Bilal told me, on the authority of Thawr ibn Zayd, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And strive in the cause of God with the striving due to Him, as you strived the first time, then Umar said, Who commanded the jihad? He said, Two tribes of Quraysh, Makhzum and Abd Shams. Then Umar said, You have spoken the truth. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Do not fear the blame of a blamer for the sake of God. He said: And that is the right of jihad. Mention who said that. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His statement, And strive in the cause of God with the striving due to Him, do not fear the blame of a blamer in God’s cause. Others said: The meaning of this is: Do what is right, do what is right. This is a statement mentioned by some of those who narrated from Al-Dahhak. The correct view of those who said this is that it refers to jihad in the way of God, because what is known about jihad is that it is most common in the saying of the speaker: I fought in the way of God, and the true meaning of jihad is to exhaust one’s energy in it. His saying: He chose you means: He chose you for His religion, and selected you to fight His enemies and strive in His cause. Ibn Zayd said about that: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said about His statement, He chose you, that he said: He guided you. And His statement: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship. God Almighty says: And your Lord has not placed upon you in the religion in which He has made you worship any hardship, for there is no way out for you from what you have been afflicted with in it, but rather He has made it easy for you and made repentance for some a way out, expiation for some, and retaliation for some. So there is no sin that a believer commits except that he has a way out for it in the religion of Islam. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: Abdul Malik bin Marwan asked Ali bin Abdullah bin Abbas about this verse: And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty. Ali bin Abdullah said: Difficulty means distress, so God made expiations a way out of that. I heard Ibn Abbas say that. He said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told me, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Yazid, he said: I heard Ibn Abbas being asked about And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty. He said: Is there anyone from Hudhayl here? A man said: Yes. He said: What do you consider a difficulty among you? He said: A narrow thing. Ibn Abbas said: So it is like that. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Ibn Abbas said: Is there anyone from Hudhayl here? A man said: I am. He also said: What do you consider to be hardship? And the rest of the hadith is similar. Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me, he said: Yahya bin Saleh told us, he said: Yahya bin Hamza told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abdullah, he said: I heard Al-Qasim bin Muhammad narrating, on the authority of Aisha, he said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. He said: It is tightness. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us: Yazid ibn Zari` told us: Abu Khalda told us: Abu al-`Aliyah said to me: Do you know what hardship is? I said: I do not know. He said: Distress, and he recited this verse: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Hammad bin Mas’adah told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty, he said: Any hardship. Amr bin Bunduq told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Khalda, who said: Abu Al-Aaliyah said to me: Do you know what hardship is? I said: No. He said: Distress. God has not made things difficult for you, nor has He placed any hardship on you in religion. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Al-Qasim, that he recited this verse: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. He said: Do you know what difficulty is? He said: Difficulty. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Yunus bin Abi Ishaq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If something in the Qur’an is foreign, then look at the poetry, for poetry is Arabic. Then Ibn Abbas called an Arab and said: What is the difficulty? He said: Difficulty. He said: You have spoken the truth. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: There is hardship in religion. He said: There is narrowness. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Others said: The meaning of this is He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty in terms of tightness in the times of your obligatory prayers if they become confusing to you, but He has made things easy for you until you are certain of their place. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Uthman ibn Bashar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty, he said: This is regarding the crescent moon of the month of Ramadan if people are in doubt about it, and regarding the Hajj if they are in doubt about the crescent moon, and regarding the Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha if they are confused about it, and the like. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And what was made difficult in Islam, rather, it was made easy. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty, meaning: He has not placed upon you in Islam any difficulty, which is broad, and it is like His statement in Al-An’am, “So whoever God wants to guide, He expands his breast to [contain] Islam. And whoever He wants to misguide, He makes his breast tight and constricted.” al-An’am 6:125 He says: Whoever He wants to misguide, He constricts his breast, and even makes Islam tight for him, although Islam is broad. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty, meaning: any narrowness, meaning: He made the religion broad, but He did not make it narrow. And His statement, the religion of your father Abraham, the word millah is in the accusative case, meaning: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty, rather He made it broad, like the word your father. So when the letter kaf was not placed in it, it was connected to the verb that preceded it, so it was in the accusative case. It is possible that its being in the accusative case is in the form of a command to it, because the speech before it is a command, so it is as if it was said: Bow and prostrate, and adhere to the religion of your father Abraham. And His saying: He named you Muslims before and in this God Almighty says: He named you, O group of those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Muslims before. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: He named you Muslims means: God named you. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata’ bin Abi Rabah told me that he heard Ibn Abbas say: God named you Muslims before. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us all, on the authority of Muammar, Qatada: He named you Muslims. He said: God named you Muslims before. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: He named you Muslims. He said: God named you. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement: He named you Muslims before, he said: God named you Muslims. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Abraham named you Muslims. They said: It is a metaphor for mentioning Abraham, peace and blessings be upon him. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: He named you Muslims. He said: Do you not see the words of Abraham: And make us Muslims to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation to You (Al-Baqarah 2:128)? He said: This is the word of Abraham: He named you Muslims. And God did not mention Islam and faith except for this nation. It was mentioned with faith and Islam together, and we have not heard of a nation mentioned except with faith. There is no basis for what Ibn Zayd said about that, because it is known that Abraham did not name the nation of Muhammad Muslims in the Qur’an, because the Qur’an was revealed a long time after him, and God Almighty said: He named you Muslims before and in this, but the one who named us Muslims before the revelation of the Qur’an, and in the Qur’an, is God who did not reveal and will not reveal. As for his saying: before, its meaning is: before the revelation of this Qur’an in the books that were revealed before it, and in this He says and in this the Book. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: He named you Muslims before and in this the Qur’an. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: Before he said: In all the books and the remembrance and in this meaning the Qur’an, and His statement: that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people God Almighty says God chose you and named you, O believers in God and His verses, from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Muslims, so that Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may be a witness over you on the Day of Resurrection, that he conveyed to you what he was sent with to you, and you will be witnesses then over all the messengers, that they conveyed to their nations what they were sent with to them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He named you Muslims before, he said: God named you Muslims before. And in this so that the Messenger may be a witness over you, that he conveyed it to you. And that you may be witnesses over the people, that their messengers conveyed it to them. And with this on the authority of Qatada, he said: This nation has been given what was given only to a prophet. It was said to the prophet: Go, for there is no blame upon you. And God said: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship. And it was said to the prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You are a witness over your people. And God said: So that you may be witnesses over the people. And it was said to the prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ask and you will be given it. And God said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: “This nation has been given three things that were given to no one except a prophet. It was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Go, for there is no blame upon you.’ God said: ‘And He has not placed upon you in religion any hardship.’ He said: It was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘You are a witness over your people.’ God said: ‘So that you may be witnesses over the people.’ It was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Ask and you will be given.’ God said: ‘Call upon Me, I will respond to you.’” (Ghafir
22:78: God the Most High means by His statement: So establish prayer and give zakat meaning: So perform the prayer that God has enjoined upon you within its limits, and give the zakat that is obligatory upon you from your wealth. And hold fast to God meaning: Trust in God and rely on Him in your affairs. Then what an excellent protector meaning: What an excellent protector God is for whoever among you does that, so establishes prayer, gives zakat, and strives in the cause of God with the striving that is due, and holds fast to Him. And what an excellent helper meaning: What an excellent helper He is for him against whoever seeks to harm him.
